title.zh: 卷八十七 列傳第二十五: 紇石烈志寧 僕散忠義 徒單合喜
title.en: Volume 87 Biographies 25: Geshiliezhining, Pusan Zhongyi, Tu Danhexi
title.raw: 卷八十七 列傳第二十五: 紇石烈志寧 僕散忠義 徒單合喜 Volume 87 Biographies 25: Geshiliezhining, Pusan Zhongyi, Tu Danhexi

sentences.zh: 紇石烈志寧

translations.literal: Geshilie Zhining
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Zhining

sentences.zh: 紇石烈志寧，本名撒曷輦，上京胡塔安人。

translations.literal: Geshilie Zhining, original name Sahelian, was a man of Hutà'an in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Zhining—whose original name was Sahelian—came from Hutà'an in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 自五代祖太尉韓赤以來，與國家世為甥舅。

translations.literal: From their fifth-generation ancestor Grand Commandant Han Chi onward, [the family] had been marriage kin with the state for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Since their fifth-generation ancestor Grand Commandant Han Chi, the family had been linked to the dynasty by marriage for generations.

sentences.zh: 父撒八，海陵時賜名懷忠，為泰州路顏河世襲謀克，轉猛安，嘗為東平尹、開遠軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Saba, during Hailing's reign was granted the name Huaizhong, served as hereditary mengke of Yanhe in Taizhou Route, was transferred to meng'an, and once held the posts of Intendant of Dongping and Military Commissioner of Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Saba received the name Huaizhong from Emperor Hailing, held the hereditary mengke post at Yanhe in Taizhou Route, rose to meng'an rank, and had served as Intendant of Dongping and as Military Commissioner of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 志寧沉毅有大略，娶梁王宗弼女永安縣主，宗弼于諸婿中最愛之。

translations.literal: Zhining was steady and resolute with great strategic vision; he married Princess Yong'an, daughter of Prince Liang Zongbi, whom Zongbi favored most among his sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining was composed, resolute, and far-sighted. He married Princess Yong'an, daughter of Prince Liang Zongbi, whom Zongbi loved best among all his sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 皇統間，為護衛。

translations.literal: During the Huangtong era he served in the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangtong period he served in the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 海陵以為右宣徽使，出為汾陽軍節度使，入為兵部尚書，改左宣徽使、都點檢，遷樞密副使，開封尹。

translations.literal: Hailing appointed him Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat; he went out as Military Commissioner of Fenyang, returned as Minister of War, was changed to Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and Chief Inspector, was transferred to Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, and Intendant of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hailing made him Right Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, then sent him out as Military Commissioner of Fenyang, recalled him as Minister of War, reassigned him as Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat and Chief Inspector, and later promoted him to Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council and Intendant of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 契丹撒八反，樞密使僕散忽土、北京留守蕭賾、西京留守蕭懷忠皆以征討無功，坐誅。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Saba rebelled, Privy Council Commissioner Pusan Hutu, Northern Capital Regent Xiao Ze, and Western Capital Regent Xiao Huaizhong were all executed for failing in the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan leader Saba rose in rebellion, Privy Council Commissioner Pusan Hutu and the regents of the Northern and Western capitals, Xiao Ze and Xiao Huaizhong, were all put to death for their failed campaigns.

sentences.zh: 於是，志寧為北面副統，與都統白彥敬，以北京、臨潢、泰州三路軍討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhining became Northern Deputy Commander-in-Chief; with Commander-in-Chief Bai Yanjing he led the armies of the Northern Capital, Linhuang, and Taizhou routes against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining was then made deputy commander of the northern front and, together with Commander-in-Chief Bai Yanjing, took the forces of the Beijing, Linhuang, and Taizhou circuits to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 志寧至北京，而海陵伐宋已渡淮。

translations.literal: When Zhining reached the Northern Capital, Hailing's campaign against Song had already crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Zhining reached the Northern Capital, Emperor Hailing's southern campaign had already carried his armies across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 彥敬、志寧聞世宗有異志，乃陰結會甯尹完顏蒲速賚、利涉軍節度使獨吉義，將攻之。

translations.literal: Yanjing and Zhining, hearing that Shizong harbored a separate design, secretly joined with Huining Intendant Wanyan Pusulai and Lishe Military Commissioner Duji Yi to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Shizong was plotting a coup, Yanjing and Zhining secretly allied with Huining Intendant Wanyan Pusulai and Lishe Military Commissioner Duji Yi and prepared to strike him.

sentences.zh: 而世宗已即位，使石抹移迭、移剌曷補來招，彥敬、志寧殺其使者九人。

translations.literal: But Shizong had already taken the throne and sent Shimoyidie and Yila Habu to summon them; Yanjing and Zhining killed nine of their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had already ascended the throne, however, and sent Shimoyidie and Yila Habu to win them over; Yanjing and Zhining killed nine of the envoys.

sentences.zh: 世宗使完顏謀衍來伐，眾不肯戰，乃與彥敬俱降。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Wanyan Moyan to attack them; the troops refused to fight, and [Zhining] surrendered together with Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong sent Wanyan Moyan against them, the army would not fight, and Zhining surrendered together with Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 世宗問曰：「正隆暴虐，人望既絕，朕以太祖之孫即大位。

translations.literal: Shizong asked, "Zhenglong was cruel and tyrannical; the people's hopes for him were exhausted. I, as a grandson of Taizu, have taken the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong questioned them: "Zhenglong was cruel and tyrannical, and the people had turned from him. I, as a grandson of Taizu, have taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 汝殺我使者，又不能為正隆死節，恐為人所圖，然後來降。

translations.literal: You killed my envoys yet could not die in loyalty to Zhenglong—fearing you would be plotted against, you then came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: You killed my envoys, yet you could not die in loyalty to Zhenglong; you feared others would plot against you and only then came to submit.

sentences.zh: 朕今殺汝等，將何辭？

translations.literal: If I now kill you, what plea will you offer?"
translations.idiomatic: If I put you to death now, what defense can you offer?"

sentences.zh: 」彥敬未有以對，志寧前奏曰：「臣等受正隆厚恩，所以不降，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: Yanjing had nothing to reply; Zhining stepped forward and said, "We received great favor from Zhenglong; that is why we did not surrender. Our crime deserves ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing had no answer. Zhining stepped forward and said, "We owed Zhenglong deep favor; that is why we would not submit. Our crime deserves death ten thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「汝輩初心亦可謂忠於所事，自今事朕，宜勉忠節。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your original intent may also be called loyalty to those you served; from now on in serving me, you should strive in loyal devotion."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your first loyalty was still loyalty to your lord. From now on, serve me with the same steadfast devotion."

sentences.zh: 世宗使紮八招窩斡，紮八乃勸之，遂稱帝。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Zhaba to summon Wowo; Zhaba instead urged him on, and Wowo thereupon declared himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong sent Zhaba to bring Wowo in, but Zhaba encouraged him instead, and Wowo thereupon declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 世宗使右副元帥完顏謀衍征之，志寧以臨海節度使，都統右翼軍。

translations.literal: Shizong sent Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Moyan to campaign against him; Zhining, as Military Commissioner of Linhai, commanded the right wing army.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong dispatched Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief Wanyan Moyan to suppress him; Zhining, serving as Military Commissioner of Linhai, commanded the army's right wing.

sentences.zh: 窩斡敗於長濼，西走，志寧追及於霿𩃭河。

translations.literal: Wowo was defeated at Changchi and fled west; Zhining overtook him at the Menglong River.
translations.idiomatic: Wowo was defeated at Changchi and fled westward; Zhining caught up with him at the Menglong River.

sentences.zh: 賊已先渡，依岸為陣，毀橋岸以為阻。

translations.literal: The rebels had already crossed first, drew up battle lines along the bank, and destroyed the bridge and shore to create obstacles.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had crossed first, formed their line along the far bank, and wrecked the bridge and shoreline to block pursuit.

sentences.zh: 志寧與賊夾河，為疑兵，與萬戶夾穀清臣、徒單海羅於下流涉渡。

translations.literal: Zhining faced the rebels across the river with a diversionary force, while with Commanders Jiagu Qingchen and Tudan Hailuo he forded downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining held the rebels in place across the river with a feint, while Commanders Jiagu Qingchen and Tudan Hailuo crossed downstream.

sentences.zh: 已渡，前有支港岸鬥絕，其中泥濘，乃束柳填藉，士卒畢濟。

translations.literal: After crossing, before them was a branch channel with steep banks and mud within; they bound willows to fill and bridge it, and the soldiers all got across.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, they found a side channel with sheer banks and deep mud; they packed it with bundled willows until every man had crossed.

sentences.zh: 行數裏，得平地，將士方食，賊奄至。

translations.literal: After marching several li they reached level ground; the officers and men had just begun to eat when the rebels suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: They marched several li to open ground, and the troops had just sat down to eat when the rebels struck without warning.

sentences.zh: 賊據南岡，三馳下志寧陣。

translations.literal: The rebels held the southern hill and charged down on Zhining's formation three times.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the southern ridge and charged Zhining's line three times.

sentences.zh: 陣堅，力戰，流矢中左臂，戰自若。

translations.literal: The formation held firm; they fought fiercely; a stray arrow struck his left arm, yet he fought as calmly as before.
translations.idiomatic: The line held. Zhining fought on fiercely; a stray arrow struck his left arm, yet he fought as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 賊據上風縱火，乘煙勢馳擊。

translations.literal: The rebels held the upwind position and set fires, then charged riding the smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels took the windward ground, set fires, and charged through the smoke.

sentences.zh: 志寧步軍繼至，轉戰十餘合，火益熾，風煙突人，不可當。

translations.literal: Zhining's infantry reinforcements arrived; they fought more than ten rounds; the fire grew fiercer; wind and smoke rushed upon the men and could not be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining's infantry came up, and the battle raged through more than ten exchanges; the flames grew hotter, wind and smoke swept into the ranks, and the position could not be held.

sentences.zh: 會雨作，風煙乃熄，遂奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Just then rain fell; the wind and smoke died away; they then pressed the attack and routed the enemy utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Rain then broke, the wind and smoke cleared, and they pressed the attack and broke the enemy completely.

sentences.zh: 於是，元帥謀衍、右監軍福壽不急擊賊，久無功，右丞僕散忠義請自討賊，而志寧擊賊有功，上以忠義代謀衍，志寧代福壽，封定國公，使蒲察通至軍中宣諭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Commander-in-Chief Moyan and Right Army Supervisor Fushou did not press the attack and long achieved nothing; Right Chancellor Pusan Zhongyi asked to campaign against the rebels himself; Zhining had merit in striking the rebels; the emperor replaced Moyan with Zhongyi and Fushou with Zhining, enfeoffed him as Duke of Dingguo, and sent Pucha Tong to the army to proclaim the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Moyan and Right Army Supervisor Fushou had been slow to press the rebels and achieved nothing for a long time. Right Chancellor Pusan Zhongyi asked to take the field himself. Because Zhining had distinguished himself in battle, the emperor replaced Moyan with Zhongyi and Fushou with Zhining, created Zhining Duke of Dingguo, and sent Pucha Tong to the army to announce the honors.

sentences.zh: 賊略懿州界，陷靈山、同昌、惠和三縣，睥睨北京。

translations.literal: The rebels raided the borders of Yizhou, captured the three counties Ling Shan, Tongchang, and Huihe, and looked toward the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels overran the Yizhou frontier, took the counties of Ling Shan, Tongchang, and Huihe, and turned their eyes toward the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 會土河水漲，賊不得渡，乃西趨三韓縣。

translations.literal: Just then the Tuhun River rose in flood and the rebels could not cross; they therefore hurried west toward Sanhan County.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuhun River was in flood and the rebels could not cross, so they hurried west toward Sanhan County.

sentences.zh: 志寧方追躡之，元帥忠義與賊遇於花道，軍頗失利。

translations.literal: Zhining was in pursuit when Commander-in-Chief Zhongyi met the rebels at Huadao and the army suffered considerable losses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining was pressing the pursuit when Commander Zhongyi met the rebels at Huadao and the army took heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 賊見志寧踵其後，不敢乘勝，遂西走。

translations.literal: The rebels, seeing Zhining close behind, did not dare press their advantage and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhining close on their heels, the rebels dared not press their advantage and fled westward.

sentences.zh: 是時，大軍馬瘦弱，不堪追襲，諸將欲止軍勿追。

translations.literal: At that time the main army's horses were weak and lean and could not sustain pursuit; the generals wished to halt the army and not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: The army's horses were exhausted and unfit for pursuit, and the generals urged a halt.

sentences.zh: 志寧獲賊候人，知賊自選精銳，與老小輜重分道，期山后會集，可擊其輜重。

translations.literal: Zhining captured a rebel scout and learned that the rebels had chosen their elite separately from the old, young, and baggage, marching by different routes to reunite beyond the mountains; their baggage train could be struck.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining captured a rebel scout and learned that the rebels had sent their picked troops ahead while families and baggage took another route, planning to reunite beyond the mountains—so their train could be attacked.

sentences.zh: 忠義以為然，遂過移馬嶺，進及嫋嶺西陷泉。

translations.literal: Zhongyi agreed; they therefore passed Yima Ridge and advanced to Xianquan west of Niaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi agreed, crossed Yima Ridge, and advanced to Xianquan west of Niaoling.

sentences.zh: 賊見左翼據南岡為陣，不敢犯。

translations.literal: The rebels saw the left wing holding the southern hill in formation and did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels saw the left wing holding the southern ridge in battle order and did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 右翼萬戶烏延查剌擊賊少卻，志寧與夾穀清臣等擊之，賊眾大敗，涉水走。

translations.literal: Right-wing Commander Wuyan Zhala struck the rebels and drove them back slightly; Zhining with Jiagu Qingchen and others attacked, and the rebel host was utterly defeated and fled wading through the water.
translations.idiomatic: Right-wing Commander Wuyan Zhala checked the rebels; Zhining and Jiagu Qingchen then struck, routing the rebel host, which fled splashing through the water.

sentences.zh: 窩斡母徐輦舉營由落括岡西去，志寧追及之，盡獲其輜重，俘五萬餘人，雜畜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Wowo's mother Xu Nian led the camp west from Luokuo Ridge; Zhining overtook them, seized all their baggage completely, captured more than fifty thousand people, and livestock beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Wowo's mother Xu Nian led the camp west from Luokuo Ridge. Zhining overtook them, seized the entire baggage train, took more than fifty thousand captives, and livestock beyond count.

sentences.zh: 偽節度使六，及其部族皆降。

translations.literal: Six false military commissioners and their clans all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Six rebel military commissioners and their clans all submitted.

sentences.zh: 窩斡走奚中，至七渡河，志寧複敗之。

translations.literal: Wowo fled into Xi territory; reaching Seven Crossings River, Zhining again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wowo fled into Xi territory; at Seven Crossings River Zhining defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 賊過渾嶺，入于奚中。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed Hun Ridge and entered Xi territory.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed Hun Ridge and withdrew deep into Xi country.

sentences.zh: 志寧獲賊將稍合住，釋弗殺，許以官賞，縱之歸，約以捕窩斡自效。

translations.literal: Zhining captured the rebel general Shaohezhu, did not kill him, promised him office and reward, released him to return, and agreed that he would capture Wowo to prove his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining captured the rebel general Shaohezhu, spared his life, promised rank and reward, and sent him back on the pledge that he would deliver Wowo.

sentences.zh: 稍合住既去，見窩斡，秘不言見獲事，乃反間奚人於窩斡曰：「陷泉失利，奚人有貳志，不可不察。

translations.literal: After Shaohezhu departed and saw Wowo, he kept secret that he had been captured and sowed dissension among the Xi against Wowo, saying, "The defeat at Xianquan shows the Xi harbor divided loyalties—you must not fail to investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Shaohezhu returned to Wowo and hid his capture, then sowed distrust among the Xi, telling Wowo, "Our defeat at Xianquan shows the Xi are wavering—you must watch them closely."

sentences.zh: 」當是時，窩斡屢敗，其下亦各有心，稍合住乃與賊帥神獨斡執窩斡，詣右都監完顏思敬降。

translations.literal: At that time Wowo had suffered repeated defeats and his followers each had their own minds; Shaohezhu then with the rebel chieftain Shenduwo seized Wowo and went to Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Sijing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wowo had already suffered defeat after defeat, and his followers were divided. Shaohezhu then joined the rebel chieftain Shenduwo, seized Wowo, and surrendered him to Right Army Supervisor Wanyan Sijing.

sentences.zh: 志寧與萬戶清臣，宗甯、速哥等，追捕餘黨至燕子城，盡得所畜善馬，因至抹拔裏達之地，悉獲之。

translations.literal: Zhining with Commanders Qingchen, Zongning, Suge, and others pursued the remaining rebels to Swallow City, obtained all the fine horses they had kept, and going on to Mobalida territory seized everything there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining, Qingchen, Zongning, Suge, and others hunted the remaining rebels to Swallow City, seized all their fine horses, and then swept Mobalida territory as well.

sentences.zh: 逆党既平，入朝，為左副元帥，賜以玉帶。

translations.literal: Once the rebel party was pacified he entered court, was made Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and was granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion crushed, he returned to court as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief and received an imperial jade belt.

sentences.zh: 經略宋事，駐軍睢陽，都元帥忠義居南京，節制諸軍。

translations.literal: He directed affairs against Song, encamped at Suiyang, while Commander-in-Chief Zhongyi resided at Nanjing and controlled all armies.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of operations against Song and encamped at Suiyang, while Commander-in-Chief Zhongyi remained at Nanjing to direct all forces.

sentences.zh: 宋將黃觀察據蔡州，楊思據潁昌。

translations.literal: The Song general Inspector Huang held Caizhou; Yang Si held Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Song officer known as Inspector Huang held Caizhou, and Yang Si held Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 志寧使完顏王祥複取蔡州，黃觀察遁去。

translations.literal: Zhining sent Wanyan Wangxiang to retake Caizhou; Inspector Huang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining sent Wanyan Wangxiang to retake Caizhou, and Inspector Huang fled.

sentences.zh: 完顏襄攻潁州，拔之，獲楊思。

translations.literal: Wanyan Xiang attacked Yingzhou, captured it, and took Yang Si.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Xiang stormed Yingzhou, took the city, and captured Yang Si.

sentences.zh: 乃移牒宋樞密使張浚，使依皇統以來舊式，浚複書曰：「謹遣使者至麾下議之。

translations.literal: He then sent a dispatch to Song Privy Council Commissioner Zhang Jun, asking that relations follow the old forms since Huangtong; Jun replied, "I respectfully send envoys to your command to discuss the matter."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Song Privy Council Commissioner Zhang Jun, urging a return to the diplomatic forms used since Huangtong. Jun replied, "I shall send envoys to your headquarters to discuss the matter."

sentences.zh: 」是時，宋得窩斡黨人括裏、紮八，用其謀攻靈璧、虹縣，都統奚撻不也叛入于宋，遂陷宿州。

translations.literal: At that time Song had obtained Wowo's followers Kuoli and Zhaba, used their plans to attack Lingbi and Hong County, and when Commander-in-Chief Xi Tabuye defected to Song, Suzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Song had taken Wowo's followers Kuoli and Zhaba, followed their advice to strike Lingbi and Hong County, and when Commander Xi Tabuye defected, Suzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 括裏等謀曰：「北人恃騎射，戰勝攻取。

translations.literal: Kuoli and the others plotted, saying, "The northerners rely on mounted archery to win battles and take cities.
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and the others argued, "The northerners depend on horse archery to win battles and storm cities.

sentences.zh: 今夏月久雨，膠解，弓不可用。

translations.literal: This summer the long rains have dissolved the glue; bows cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: This summer the rains have lasted so long that bow glue has softened and their bows are useless."

sentences.zh: 」故李世輔與之來攻宿州。

translations.literal: Therefore Li Shifu came with them to attack Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Li Shifu joined them in the attack on Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 歸德尹術甲撒速、宿州防禦使烏林答剌撒、萬戶溫蒂罕速可、裴滿婁室，不守約束，不肯堅壁俟大軍，輒出與戰，由是軍敗，城陷。

translations.literal: Guide Intendant Shujia Sasu, Suzhou Defense Commissioner Ulinada Lasa, Commander Wendihan Suke, and Peiman Loushi did not keep discipline, refused to hold the walls and await the main army, but went out to fight; thereby the army was defeated and the city lost.
translations.idiomatic: Guide Intendant Shujia Sasu, Suzhou Defense Commissioner Ulinada Lasa, Commander Wendihan Suke, and Peiman Loushi ignored orders, refused to hold the walls until the main force arrived, and sallied out to fight; the army was beaten and the city lost.

sentences.zh: 剌撒嘗遣人入宋界貿易，交通李世輔，受其賂遺，久之，事覺，伏誅。

translations.literal: Lasa had once sent men into Song territory to trade, communicated with Li Shifu, and accepted bribes from him; after a long time the matter was discovered and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Lasa had sent men into Song territory to trade, maintained contact with Li Shifu, and accepted his bribes; when the affair came to light he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 謀克賽一坐故知不舉，除名。

translations.literal: Mengke Saiyi, for knowing and not reporting, was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Mengke Saiyi, who had known of the dealings but failed to report them, was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 撻不也母斡裏懶，緣坐當死，上曰：「撻不也背國棄母，殺之何益？

translations.literal: Tabuye's mother Wolilan, implicated by association, was due to die; the emperor said, "Tabuye betrayed the state and abandoned his mother—what good would killing her do?
translations.idiomatic: Tabuye's mother Wolilan was implicated and sentenced to death. The emperor said, "Tabuye betrayed his country and abandoned his mother—what good would it do to kill her?

sentences.zh: 朕閔其老。

translations.literal: I pity her age."
translations.idiomatic: I pity her for her age."

sentences.zh: 」遂原其死。

translations.literal: Her death was therefore pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Her sentence was remitted.

sentences.zh: 詔撒速、剌撒、速可、婁室各杖有差，撒速、剌撒仍解職。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sasu, Lasa, Suke, and Loushi each flogged in varying degrees; Sasu and Lasa were also removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Sasu, Lasa, Suke, and Loushi were ordered flogged in varying degrees, and Sasu and Lasa were also dismissed from their posts.

sentences.zh: 世輔自以為得志，日與括裏、紮八置酒高會。

translations.literal: Shifu, thinking himself triumphant, daily held grand banquets with Kuoli and Zhaba.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu, flush with success, held lavish banquets every day with Kuoli and Zhaba.

sentences.zh: 志寧以精兵萬人，發自睢陽，趨宿州。

translations.literal: Zhining with ten thousand elite troops set out from Suiyang and hastened to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining marched from Suiyang with ten thousand picked troops toward Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 中使來督軍，志寧附奏曰：「此役不煩聖慮，臣但恐世輔遁去耳。

translations.literal: An imperial envoy came to urge the army forward; Zhining appended a memorial saying, "This campaign need not trouble Your Majesty's concern; I only fear that Shifu may escape."
translations.idiomatic: When an imperial envoy came to hurry the army forward, Zhining added a note: "This battle need not trouble Your Majesty; I only fear that Shifu may slip away."

sentences.zh: 」世輔聞志寧軍止萬人，甚易之，曰：「當令十人執一人也。

translations.literal: Shifu, hearing Zhining's army was only ten thousand, thought it very easy and said, "Ten men should be enough to seize one."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Zhining had only ten thousand men, Shifu thought the odds laughable and said, "Ten of ours ought to take one of theirs."

sentences.zh: 」括裏等問候人所見上將旗幟，知是志寧，謂世輔曰：「此撒合輦監軍也，軍至萬人，慎毋輕之。

translations.literal: Kuoli and the others questioned the scouts about the commander's banners and, knowing it was Zhining, told Shifu, "This is Sahelian the army supervisor; though his force is only ten thousand, you must not take him lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Kuoli and the others questioned the scouts about the command banners, recognized Zhining, and warned Shifu, "That is Sahelian himself in command. Even with only ten thousand men, do not underestimate him."

sentences.zh: 」大定三年五月二十日，志寧將至宿州，乃令從軍盡執旗幟，駐州西為疑兵，三猛安兵駐州南。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the fifth month of the third year of Dading, as Zhining was about to reach Suzhou, he ordered all followers to carry banners, encamped west of the city as a diversion, and posted three meng'an forces south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth day of the fifth month in the third year of Dading, as Zhining approached Suzhou, he had every man raise banners west of the city as a feint and posted three meng'an units to the south.

sentences.zh: 志寧自以大軍駐州東南，厄其歸路。

translations.literal: Zhining himself stationed the main army southeast of the city to block the enemy's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining himself took the main force to the southeast and cut off the enemy's retreat.

sentences.zh: 世輔望見州西兵旌旗蔽野，果謂大軍在州西，而謂東南兵少不足慮，先擊之。

translations.literal: Shifu, seeing west of the city banners covering the fields, indeed thought the main army was west of the city and that the few troops to the southeast were not worth concern; he attacked them first.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu saw the banners west of the city covering the plain, assumed the main Jin force was there, dismissed the smaller force to the southeast, and struck it first.

sentences.zh: 以步騎數萬，皆執盾，背城為陣，外以行馬捍之。

translations.literal: With tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry, all bearing shields, he drew up a formation with his back to the city and protected the front with field barriers.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry with shields, formed his line with the city at his back, and screened the front with field barriers.

sentences.zh: 使別將將兵三千，出自東門，欲自陣後攻志寧軍，萬戶蒲查擊敗之。

translations.literal: He sent a separate commander with three thousand troops out the east gate to strike Zhining's army from the rear; Commander Pucha defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a secondary commander with three thousand men out the east gate to hit Zhining from behind, but Commander Pucha routed them.

sentences.zh: 右翼萬戶夾穀清臣為前行，撤毀行馬，短兵接戰，世輔軍亂，諸將乘之，追殺至城下。

translations.literal: Right-wing Commander Jiagu Qingchen led the van, tore down the field barriers, and closed in hand to hand; Shifu's army fell into disorder; the generals pressed the advantage and pursued to the foot of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Right-wing Commander Jiagu Qingchen led the van, tore down the barriers, and closed for hand-to-hand fighting. Shifu's army broke, the Jin generals pressed the attack, and the pursuit reached the city wall.

sentences.zh: 是夕，世輔盡按敗將，將斬之，其統制常吉懼而來奔，盡得城中虛實。

translations.literal: That evening Shifu assembled all the defeated officers and was about to execute them; his controller Chang Ji, in fear, came over to the Jin side and revealed everything about conditions in the city.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shifu lined up his defeated officers for execution. His controller Chang Ji, terrified, defected and told the Jin everything about the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 明日，世輔悉兵出戰，騎兵居前，志寧使夾穀清臣當之。

translations.literal: The next day Shifu brought out his entire army; cavalry led the way, and Zhining had Jiagu Qingchen meet them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shifu committed his whole army with cavalry in the van; Zhining sent Jiagu Qingchen to meet them.

sentences.zh: 世輔別將以五六千騎為一隊，與清臣遇，清臣踵擊之，宋將不能反旆。

translations.literal: Shifu's subordinate commanders advanced in units of five or six thousand horsemen; meeting Qingchen, Qingchen pressed them from behind and the Song officers could not turn their standards back.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu's subordinates came up in bodies of five or six thousand horsemen. Qingchen struck them from behind and drove them so hard the Song commanders could not wheel about.

sentences.zh: 志寧麾諸軍力戰，世輔複大敗，走者自相蹈藉，僵屍相枕，爭城門而入。

translations.literal: Zhining directed all armies to fight fiercely; Shifu was again utterly defeated; fugitives trampled one another, corpses lay piled atop corpses, and all struggled for the city gates to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining drove every unit into the fight. Shifu was routed again. Fugitives trampled one another, corpses lay in heaps, and men fought to squeeze through the gates.

sentences.zh: 門填塞，人人自阻，遂緣城而上。

translations.literal: The gates were jammed; each man blocked the others, and they therefore climbed the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The gates clogged and men blocked one another, so they scrambled up the walls instead.

sentences.zh: 我軍自濠外射之，往往墮死於隍間。

translations.literal: Our army shot at them from beyond the moat; many fell dead into the ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Jin archers shot from beyond the moat, and many Song soldiers fell dead into the ditch below.

sentences.zh: 殺騎士萬五千，步卒三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Fifteen thousand horsemen and more than thirty thousand foot soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen thousand cavalry and more than thirty thousand infantry were killed.

sentences.zh: 世輔乘夜脫走。

translations.literal: Shifu escaped under cover of night.
translations.idiomatic: Shifu slipped away under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 明日，夾穀清臣、張師忠追及世輔，斬首四千余，赴水死者不可勝計，獲甲三萬，他兵仗甚眾。

translations.literal: The next day Jiagu Qingchen and Zhang Shizhong overtook Shifu, beheaded more than four thousand, and those who drowned were beyond counting; thirty thousand suits of armor were captured, and other weapons in great quantity.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jiagu Qingchen and Zhang Shizhong caught Shifu, took more than four thousand heads, and drowned so many that the number could not be counted. They seized thirty thousand suits of armor and a vast store of other arms.

sentences.zh: 上以禦服金線袍、玉吐鶻、賓鐵佩刀，使移剌道就軍中賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yila Dao to the army to bestow on him an imperial gold-thread robe, jade hunting hawk, and treasured steel belt knife.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yila Dao to the camp with an imperial gold-thread robe, a jade hunting hawk, and a treasured steel belt knife.

sentences.zh: 凡有功將士，猛安、謀克並如陝西遷賞，蒲輦進官三階、重彩三端、絹六匹，旗鼓笛手、吏人各賜錢十貫。

translations.literal: All meritorious officers and soldiers: meng'an and mengke were rewarded as in the Shaanxi campaign; pulian received three ranks of promotion, three bolts of fine silk, and six bolts of plain silk; banner-drummers, pipers, and clerks each received ten strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer and soldier who had earned merit was rewarded on the scale used in the Shaanxi campaign. Pulian officers were promoted three ranks and given three bolts of fine silk and six of plain silk; drummers, pipers, and clerks each received ten strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 詔志寧曰：「卿雖年少，前征契丹戰功居最，今複破大敵，朕甚嘉之。」

translations.literal: An edict to Zhining said, "Though you are still young, in the former campaign against the Khitan your merit ranked first; now you have again broken a great enemy—I greatly commend you."
translations.idiomatic: An edict told Zhining, "You are still young, yet in the Khitan campaign your merit ranked first, and now you have broken a great enemy again. I am deeply pleased."

sentences.zh: 宋人議和不能決，都元帥僕散忠義移軍泰和，志寧移軍臨渙，遂渡淮，徒單克寧取盱眙、濠、廬、和、滁等州。

translations.literal: The Song could not settle on peace; Commander-in-Chief Pusan Zhongyi moved his army to Taihe, Zhining moved to Linhuan, then crossed the Huai; Tudan Kening took Xuyi, Hao, Lu, He, Chu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Song could not agree on peace terms. Commander Pusan Zhongyi shifted to Taihe, Zhining to Linhuan, and the Jin crossed the Huai. Tudan Kening took Xuyi, Hao, Lu, He, Chu, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋人懼，乃決意請和。

translations.literal: The Song were afraid and thereupon resolved to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the Song at last resolved to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 使者六七往反，議遂定，宋世為侄國，約歲幣二十萬兩、匹。

translations.literal: Envoys went back and forth six or seven times; the terms were settled: the Song dynasty was to be a nephew state and annual tribute was set at two hundred thousand taels and bolts.
translations.idiomatic: After six or seven rounds of envoys the terms were fixed: the Song would accept nephew-state status and pay annual tribute of two hundred thousand taels and bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 魏杞奉誓書入見，複通好。

translations.literal: Wei Qi presented the oath document and entered audience; friendly relations were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qi presented the sworn treaty and was received at court, and friendly relations were restored.

sentences.zh: 志寧還軍睢陽，上以禦服、玉佩刀、通犀禦帶賜之。

translations.literal: Zhining returned the army to Suiyang; the emperor bestowed on him imperial robes, a jade belt knife, and an imperial rhinoceros-horn belt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining brought the army back to Suiyang, and the emperor gave him imperial robes, a jade belt knife, and a rhinoceros-horn imperial belt.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「靈璧、虹縣、宿州兵士死者，朕實閔焉。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The soldiers who died at Lingbi, Hong County, and Suzhou—I truly grieve for them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The soldiers who fell at Lingbi, Hong County, and Suzhou weigh on my heart.

sentences.zh: 宜歸葬鄉里，官為齎送，人賻錢三十貫。

translations.literal: They should be returned for burial in their home districts; officials shall convey the remains, and each person shall receive thirty strings of cash as condolence payment."
translations.idiomatic: Let them be sent home for burial, with officials to convey the remains, and let each family receive thirty strings of cash in condolence."

sentences.zh: 」鳳翔尹孛術魯定方以下猛安謀克，官為致祭。

translations.literal: From Fengxiang Intendant Boshulu Dingfang down, meng'an and mengke were to have officials perform the sacrifices on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: From Fengxiang Intendant Boshulu Dingfang down through the meng'an and mengke ranks, officials were to perform the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 定方賻銀五百兩、重彩二十端，猛安三百貫，謀克二百貫，蒲裏衍一百貫，權猛安二百貫，權謀克一百五十貫，權蒲裏衍七十貫。

translations.literal: Dingfang's condolence gift was five hundred taels of silver and twenty bolts of fine silk; meng'an three hundred strings, mengke two hundred, puliyan one hundred, acting meng'an two hundred, acting mengke one hundred fifty, acting puliyan seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang was to receive five hundred taels of silver and twenty bolts of fine silk; meng'an three hundred strings, mengke two hundred, puliyan one hundred, acting meng'an two hundred, acting mengke one hundred fifty, and acting puliyan seventy.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，忠義朝京師，志寧駐軍南京。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Zhongyi attended court in the capital; Zhining encamped at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Zhongyi went to the capital, while Zhining kept the army at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 五月，志寧召至京師，拜平章政事，左副元帥如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Zhining was summoned to the capital, appointed Grand Councilor, and retained his post as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhining was recalled to the capital, made Grand Councilor, and kept his rank as Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 志寧複還軍，賜玉束帶，上曰：「卿壯年能立功如此，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhining again returned to the army and was granted a jade belt; the emperor said, "In your vigorous years you can achieve merit such as this—I greatly commend you.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining returned to the army again and received a jade belt. The emperor said, "In the prime of your life you have won such merit—I am deeply pleased.

sentences.zh: 南服雖定，日月尚淺，須卿一往規畫。

translations.literal: Though the south has been pacified, little time has passed; you must go once to plan and arrange.
translations.idiomatic: The south may be pacified, but order there is still new—you must go once and set things in order.

sentences.zh: 」六年二月，志寧還京師，拜樞密使。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Zhining returned to the capital and was appointed Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he returned to the capital and was made Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 七年十一月八日，皇太子生日，宴群臣於東宮，志寧奉觴上壽，上悅，顧謂太子曰：「天下無事，吾父子今日相樂，皆此人力也。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the eleventh month of the seventh year, the crown prince's birthday, the emperor feasted the ministers in the Eastern Palace; Zhining offered a toast for long life; the emperor was pleased and, turning to the prince, said, "Under heaven all is at peace; that you and I can rejoice together today is all this man's doing.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the eleventh month in the seventh year, at the crown prince's birthday feast in the Eastern Palace, Zhining raised a toast for long life. The emperor was pleased and told the prince, "The realm is at peace; that we can feast together today is his doing alone."

sentences.zh: 」使太子取御前玉大杓酌酒，上手飲志寧，即以玉杓及黃金五百兩賜之。

translations.literal: He had the prince take the great jade ladle before the throne to pour wine; the emperor drank from Zhining's hand and thereupon bestowed the jade ladle and five hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: He had the prince pour wine with the great jade ladle from the imperial table; the emperor drank with Zhining and then gave him the ladle and five hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 以第十四女下嫁志寧子諸神奴，八年十月，進幣，宴百官于慶和殿。

translations.literal: The fourteenth princess was given in marriage to Zhining's son Zhushennu; in the tenth month of the eighth year the betrothal gifts were presented and all officials were feasted in the Hall of Celebrated Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's fourteenth daughter was married to Zhining's son Zhushennu. In the tenth month of the eighth year the betrothal gifts were presented and the court feasted in the Hall of Celebrated Harmony.

sentences.zh: 皇女以婦禮謁見，志寧夫婦坐而受之，歡飲終日，夜久乃罷。

translations.literal: The imperial daughter paid her respects in the manner of a daughter-in-law; Zhining and his wife sat and received them; they feasted joyfully all day and only late at night dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The princess greeted them as a daughter-in-law should; Zhining and his wife sat to receive her. The celebration lasted all day and deep into the night.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜右丞相。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，代宗敘北征。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he replaced Zongxu on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he took Zongxu's place on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 既還，遣使者迎勞，賜以弓矢、玉吐鶻。

translations.literal: After his return, envoys were sent to welcome and reward him; he was granted bows and arrows and a jade hunting hawk.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor sent envoys to welcome him and gave him bows, arrows, and a jade hunting hawk.

sentences.zh: 入見，上慰勞良久。

translations.literal: He entered audience; the emperor comforted him at length.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received at court the emperor comforted him at length.

sentences.zh: 是日，封廣平郡王，複遣使就第慰勞之。

translations.literal: That same day he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping; envoys were again sent to his residence to console and reward him.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was created Prince of Guangping, and envoys were sent again to his home with further rewards.

sentences.zh: 皇太子生日，宴群臣於東宮，以玉帶賜志寧，上曰：「此梁王宗弼所服者，故以賜卿。

translations.literal: On the crown prince's birthday the emperor feasted the ministers in the Eastern Palace and bestowed a jade belt on Zhining, saying, "This is what Prince Liang Zongbi wore; I therefore give it to you.
translations.idiomatic: At the crown prince's birthday feast in the Eastern Palace the emperor gave Zhining a jade belt and said, "Prince Liang Zongbi once wore this; I give it to you now."

sentences.zh: 」郊祀覃恩，從征護衛，皆有賜，進封金源郡王。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice amnesty, those who had accompanied the campaign in the Imperial Guard all received gifts; he was advanced to Prince of Jinyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice amnesty, guards who had joined the campaign were rewarded, and he was advanced to Prince of Jinyuan.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義，本名烏者，上京拔盧古河人，宣獻皇后侄，元妃之兄也。

translations.literal: Pusan Zhongyi, original name Wuzhe, was a man of Balugu River in the Upper Capital, nephew of Empress Xuanxian, and elder brother of the Primary Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Zhongyi—original name Wuzhe—came from Balugu River in the Upper Capital. He was a nephew of Empress Xuanxian and elder brother of the Primary Consort.

sentences.zh: 高祖斡魯補。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Wolubu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was Wolubu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖班睹。

translations.literal: Great-great-grandfather Bandu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandfather was Bandu.

sentences.zh: 祖胡闌。

translations.literal: Grandfather Hulan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Hulan.

sentences.zh: 父背魯，國初世襲謀克，婆速路統軍使，致仕。

translations.literal: Father Beilu, hereditary mengke at the founding of the state, Commander of the Basu Route, retired.
translations.idiomatic: His father Beilu held a hereditary mengke post at the dynasty's founding, served as commander of the Basu Route, and later retired.

sentences.zh: 忠義魁偉，長髯，喜談兵，有大略。

translations.literal: Zhongyi was imposing in stature, with a long beard; he delighted in discussing military affairs and possessed great strategic vision.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi was tall and imposing, wore a long beard, loved to talk of war, and had a strategist's mind.

sentences.zh: 年十六，領本謀克兵，從宗輔定陝西，行間射中宋大將，宋兵遂潰，由是知名。

translations.literal: At sixteen he led his own mengke troops, followed Zongfu in pacifying Shaanxi, and in the midst of battle shot a great Song general; the Song army thereupon broke; from this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he led his mengke troops under Zongfu in the pacification of Shaanxi, shot a major Song commander in the heat of battle, and routed the Song army—his fame dates from that day.

sentences.zh: 帥府錄其功，承制署為謀克。

translations.literal: The commandery headquarters recorded his merit and, by imperial order, appointed him mengke.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters recorded his merit and appointed him mengke by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 宗弼再取河南，表薦忠義為猛安。

translations.literal: When Zongbi again took Henan, he memorialized recommending Zhongyi as meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi campaigned in Henan again, he recommended Zhongyi for meng'an rank.

sentences.zh: 攻冀州，先登，攻大名府，以本部兵力戰，破其軍十余萬，賞以奴婢、馬牛、金銀、重彩。

translations.literal: Attacking Jizhou he was first to scale the walls; attacking Daming Prefecture, with his own unit he fought fiercely and broke an enemy army of more than a hundred thousand; he was rewarded with slaves, cattle, silver, gold, and fine silk.
translations.idiomatic: At Jizhou he was first over the wall; at Daming he broke an enemy force of more than a hundred thousand with his own troops and was rewarded with slaves, livestock, silver, gold, and fine silk.

sentences.zh: 從宗弼渡淮攻壽、廬等州，宗弼稱之曰：「此子勇略過人，將帥之器也。

translations.literal: Following Zongbi he crossed the Huai to attack Shou, Lu, and other prefectures; Zongbi praised him, saying, "This man's courage and strategy surpass others; he has the makings of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zongbi across the Huai against Shou, Lu, and other prefectures. Zongbi said of him, "His courage and strategy surpass ordinary men; he has the makings of a commander."

sentences.zh: 」賞馬五匹、牛一百五十頭、羊五百口，領親軍萬戶，超甯遠大將軍，承其父世襲謀克。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with five horses, one hundred fifty oxen, and five hundred sheep, was made commander of ten thousand household guards, was promoted to Grand General of Ningyuan, and inherited his father's hereditary mengke post.
translations.idiomatic: He received five horses, one hundred fifty oxen, and five hundred sheep, was made commander of the ten-thousand-household guard, promoted to Grand General of Ningyuan, and inherited his father's hereditary mengke post.

sentences.zh: 皇統四年，除博州防禦使，公餘學女直字，及古演算法，閱月，盡能通之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Huangtong he was appointed Defense Commissioner of Bozhou; in his spare time he studied Jurchen script and ancient calculation methods, and within a month mastered them completely.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Huangtong he became Defense Commissioner of Bozhou. In his spare time he studied Jurchen script and classical mathematics and mastered both within a month.

sentences.zh: 在郡不事田獵、燕遊，以職業為務，郡中翕然稱治。

translations.literal: In the prefecture he did not engage in hunting or banqueting but devoted himself to duty; the whole commandery came to praise his good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He did not hunt or feast in office but devoted himself to his duties, and the whole commandery came to praise his governance.

sentences.zh: 忽一夕陰晦，囚徒謀為反獄。

translations.literal: Suddenly one night the sky grew dark; the prisoners plotted to break out of jail.
translations.idiomatic: One night the sky turned dark and the prisoners plotted a jailbreak.

sentences.zh: 倉猝間，將校皆惶駭失措，忠義從容，但使守更吏撾鼓鳴角。

translations.literal: In the sudden crisis the officers were all alarmed and at a loss; Zhongyi remained composed and simply had the watch officers beat the drum and sound the horn.
translations.idiomatic: Officers panicked in the crisis, but Zhongyi stayed calm and had the watch officers beat the drum and sound the horn.

sentences.zh: 囚徒以為天且曉，不敢出，自就桎梏。

translations.literal: The prisoners thought dawn was near and did not dare come out, but returned of themselves to their fetters.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners thought dawn had come, dared not break out, and returned quietly to their shackles.

sentences.zh: 及考，郡民詣闕願留，詔從之。

translations.literal: At the time of his evaluation the people of the commandery went to court asking that he be retained; an edict granted their request.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was reviewed the people petitioned the throne to keep him, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 八年，改同知真定尹，兼河北西路兵馬都總管，遷西北路招討使，入為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was changed to Vice Intendant of Zhending and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Western Hebei Route army, transferred to Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner, and entered court as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Vice Intendant of Zhending and commander of Western Hebei forces, then Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner, and finally Minister of War at court.

sentences.zh: 僕散忽土嘗與海陵篡立，恃勢陵傲同列，忠義因會飲眾辱之，海陵不悅，出為震武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Pusan Hutu had once joined Hailing in usurping the throne and, relying on his power, looked down on his peers; Zhongyi humiliated him before the assembled company at a banquet; Hailing was displeased and sent him out as Military Commissioner of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Hutu had helped Hailing seize the throne and bullied his colleagues. Zhongyi publicly humiliated him at a banquet. Hailing was displeased and sent Zhongyi out as Military Commissioner of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 火山賊李鐵槍乘暑來攻，忠義單衣從一騎迎擊之，射殺數人，賊乃退。

translations.literal: The Huoshan bandit Li Tieqiang attacked in the heat of summer; Zhongyi in a single garment with one horse went out to meet them, shot and killed several men, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Huoshan bandit Li Tieqiang attacked in summer heat. Zhongyi rode out alone in light dress, killed several men, and drove the bandits off.

sentences.zh: 改臨洮尹，兼熙秦路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: He was changed to Intendant of Lin Tao and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of the Xi-Qin Route army.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Intendant of Lin Tao and commander of Xi-Qin forces.

sentences.zh: 海陵召至京師謂之曰：「洮河地接吐蕃、木波，異時剽害良民，州縣不能制。

translations.literal: Hailing summoned him to the capital and said to him, "The Tao River region borders Tibet and Mubo; in former times they raided and harmed good people, and the prefectures and counties could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing summoned him to the capital and said, "The Tao River frontier borders Tibet and Mubo. Raiders have long harried the people while local officials could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 汝宿將，故以命汝。

translations.literal: You are a veteran commander; I therefore appoint you.
translations.idiomatic: You are a veteran; that is why I send you.

sentences.zh: 」賜條服、玉具、佩刀。

translations.literal: He was granted a ceremonial robe, jade fittings, and a belt knife.
translations.idiomatic: He received a ceremonial robe, jade fittings, and an imperial belt knife.

sentences.zh: 閱再考，徙平陽尹，再徙濟南尹。

translations.literal: After a second evaluation he was transferred to Intendant of Pingyang, then again to Intendant of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: After a second review he was moved to Pingyang, then to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 以本官為漢南路行營副統制，伐宋，克通化軍。

translations.literal: With his existing office he served as Deputy Commander of the Southern Han Route field headquarters in the campaign against Song and captured Tonghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy commander of the Southern Han field headquarters in the Song campaign and captured Tonghua Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，海陵死揚州，罷兵入朝京師，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Hailing died at Yangzhou, the army was halted, he entered the capital, and was appointed Right Vice Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded, Hailing died at Yangzhou, the armies withdrew, Zhongyi entered the capital, and was made Right Vice Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 移剌窩斡忄栗號，兵久不決。

translations.literal: Yila Wowo declared himself [emperor]; the campaign dragged on without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Yila Wowo had declared himself ruler, and the campaign dragged on without result.

sentences.zh: 右副元帥完顏謀衍既敗之於霿𩃭河，乃擁眾，貪鹵掠，不追討，而縱其子斜哥暴橫軍中，士卒不用命。

translations.literal: Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Moyan, having defeated him at the Menglong River, then amassed troops, greedily plundered booty, did not pursue, and allowed his son Xiege to act violently in the army; the soldiers would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Right Deputy Commander Wanyan Moyan, after defeating Wowo at the Menglong River, let his men plunder instead of pursuing, and allowed his son Xiege to terrorize the army until the troops would not obey.

sentences.zh: 賊得水草善地，官軍踵其遺餘，水草乏，馬益弱，賊軼出山西，久無功。

translations.literal: The rebels obtained good pasture and water; the government army followed their leavings; pasture and water were scarce and the horses grew weaker; the rebels outran them west of the mountains; for a long time there was no success.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the good pasture; government forces trailed their leavings through barren ground, horses weakened, and the rebels outpaced them west of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 忠義請曰：「契丹小寇，不時殄滅，致煩聖慮。

translations.literal: Zhongyi requested, saying, "A petty Khitan bandit, if not destroyed in time, has troubled Your Majesty's concern.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi petitioned, "This petty Khitan band has troubled Your Majesty too long.

sentences.zh: 臣聞主憂臣辱，願效死力除之。

translations.literal: I have heard that when the ruler grieves the subject is shamed; I wish to offer my life's strength to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler worries, the subject should be ashamed. Let me devote my life to destroying them."

sentences.zh: 」世宗大悅。

translations.literal: Shizong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 即召還謀衍，勒歸斜哥本貫。

translations.literal: Moyan was immediately recalled; Xiege was ordered back to his native register.
translations.idiomatic: Moyan was recalled at once and Xiege was sent back to his home register.

sentences.zh: 拜忠義平章政事，兼右副元帥，封榮國公，賜以禦府貂裘、賓鐵吐鶻弓矢大刀、具裝對馬及安山鐵甲、金牌，詔曰：「軍中將士有犯，連職之外並以軍法從事，有功者依格遷賞。

translations.literal: Zhongyi was appointed Grand Councilor and concurrently Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Rongguo, granted an imperial sable coat, treasured steel hunting hawk with bow, arrows, and great knife, fully armored paired horses and Anshan iron armor, and a gold tablet; an edict said, "If officers and soldiers in the army commit offenses, beyond their linked offices they are all subject to military law; those with merit are promoted and rewarded according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi was made Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander, created Duke of Rongguo, and given an imperial sable coat, steel bow and hunting hawk, great knife, armored horses, Anshan iron armor, and a gold tablet. The edict said officers who offended were subject to military law, and merit would be rewarded by regulation.

sentences.zh: 」詔諸將士曰：「兵久駐邊陲，蠹費財用，百姓不得休息。

translations.literal: An edict to all officers and soldiers said, "The army has long been stationed on the frontier, wasting resources; the people cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told the troops, "Long service on the frontier has wasted treasure and worn the people down.

sentences.zh: 今以右丞忠義為平章政事、右副元帥，宜同心戮力，無或弛慢。

translations.literal: Now Right Vice Chancellor Zhongyi is Grand Councilor and Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief; you should join hearts and exert your strength, and must not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Chancellor Zhongyi is now Grand Councilor and deputy commander. Unite in purpose and do not slacken."

sentences.zh: 」忠義至軍，賊陷靈山、同昌、惠和等縣，陣而西行。

translations.literal: When Zhongyi reached the army, the rebels had captured Ling Shan, Tongchang, Huihe, and other counties and were drawing up battle lines marching west.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyi reached the army, the rebels had taken Ling Shan, Tongchang, Huihe, and other counties and were marching west in battle order.

sentences.zh: 忠義追之，及於花道，宗亨為左翼，宗敘為右翼，與賊夾河而陣。

translations.literal: Zhongyi pursued them and overtook them at Huadao; Zongheng was the left wing, Zongxu the right wing, and they drew up battle lines facing the rebels across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi pursued them to Huadao. Zongheng commanded the left wing, Zongxu the right, and they formed line across the river from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊渡河，先攻左翼，偏敗，右翼救之，賊引去。

translations.literal: The rebels crossed the river and first attacked the left wing, which was partially defeated; the right wing rescued them and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels crossed and struck the left wing first, which buckled; the right wing rescued it and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 窩斡乃以精銳自隨，以羸兵護其母妻輜重由別道西走，期於山后會集。

translations.literal: Wowo then took his elite with him while weak troops guarded his mother, wife, and baggage by a separate route west, planning to reunite beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wowo took his elite with him while weak troops escorted his family and baggage by another road west, planning to reunite beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 追複及於嫋嶺西陷泉。

translations.literal: The pursuit again overtook them at Xianquan west of Niaoling.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit caught them again at Xianquan west of Niaoling.

sentences.zh: 與賊遇，時昏霧四塞，跬步莫睹物色，忠義禱曰：「狂寇肆暴，殺戮無辜，天不助惡，當為開霽。

translations.literal: Meeting the rebels, at that time dark mist filled all four sides and one could not see a thing within a few steps; Zhongyi prayed, saying, "This mad band runs wild and slaughters the innocent; Heaven does not aid evil—may it clear the mist.
translations.idiomatic: They met the rebels in fog so thick they could not see a pace ahead. Zhongyi prayed, "This band slaughters the innocent. Heaven does not aid evil—clear the mist."

sentences.zh: 」奠已，昏霧廓然。

translations.literal: When the offering was complete, the dark mist suddenly cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When the offering was finished the fog lifted at once.

sentences.zh: 及戰，忠義左據南岡，為偃月陣，右迤而北，大敗之，獲其弟嫋，俘生口三十萬，獲雜畜十余萬，車帳金珍以钜萬計，悉分諸軍。

translations.literal: In battle Zhongyi's left held the southern hill in a crescent formation, the right swept northward, and utterly defeated them; they captured his younger brother Niao, took three hundred thousand captives, more than a hundred thousand head of livestock, and carts, tents, gold, and treasures reckoned in tens of thousands—all were divided among the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Zhongyi's left held the southern ridge in a crescent formation while the right swept north and broke the enemy. They took his brother Niao, three hundred thousand captives, vast herds, and treasure beyond count, all divided among the troops.

sentences.zh: 賊走趨奚地，遣將追躡，至七渡河，又敗之。

translations.literal: The rebels fled toward Xi territory; generals were sent in pursuit and at Seven Crossings River defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Xi country; pursuers overtook them at Seven Crossings River and defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 既逾渾嶺，複進軍襲之，望風奔潰，遁入奚中，降者相屬於路。

translations.literal: Having crossed Hun Ridge they advanced again to strike them; at sight of the army they fled in panic, scattering into Xi territory, and those who surrendered lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed Hun Ridge and struck again; the rebels broke at sight of the army and fled into Xi country, surrendering all along the road.

sentences.zh: 詔忠義曰：「卿材能素著，果能大破賊眾，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: An edict to Zhongyi said, "Your ability has long been evident; you have indeed broken the rebel host greatly—I greatly commend you.
translations.idiomatic: An edict told Zhongyi, "Your ability is well known, and you have broken the rebel host—I am deeply pleased."

sentences.zh: 今遣勞卿，如朕親往。

translations.literal: Now I send envoys to console you as if I came in person.
translations.idiomatic: I send envoys to honor you as if I came myself.

sentences.zh: 賜卿禦衣、及骨睹犀具佩刀、通犀帶等。

translations.literal: I bestow on you imperial robes, a bone-rhinoceros fitted belt knife, and an imperial rhinoceros-horn belt, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Take imperial robes, a bone-rhinoceros belt knife, a rhinoceros-horn belt, and the like.

sentences.zh: 就以俘獲，均散軍士。

translations.literal: With the captives taken, distribute them evenly among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the captives evenly among the soldiers."

sentences.zh: 」窩斡既敗，遂入于奚中。

translations.literal: Wowo having been defeated, then entered Xi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Wowo, defeated, withdrew into Xi country.

sentences.zh: 高忠建敗奚於栲栳山，移剌道取抹白諸奚之家，抹白奚乃降，窩斡勢益弱。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongjian defeated the Xi at Kaolaoshan; Yila Dao took the households of the Mobai Xi; the Mobai Xi then surrendered, and Wowo's strength grew ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongjian defeated the Xi at Kaolao Mountain; Yila Dao seized Mobai Xi households; the Mobai Xi submitted, and Wowo grew weaker.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈志寧獲賊將稍合住，縱之使歸，約以捕窩斡自贖，仍許以官賞。

translations.literal: Geshilie Zhining captured the rebel general Shaohezhu, released him to return, agreed that he would capture Wowo to redeem himself, and still promised office and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Zhining captured Shaohezhu, released him, and promised rank and reward if he delivered Wowo.

sentences.zh: 稍合住與其黨，執窩斡詣完顏思敬降。

translations.literal: Shaohezhu with his faction seized Wowo and went to Wanyan Sijing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohezhu and his men seized Wowo and surrendered him to Wanyan Sijing.

sentences.zh: 契丹平。

translations.literal: The Khitan rebellion was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan rebellion was ended.

sentences.zh: 忠義朝京師，拜尚書右丞相，改封沂國公，以玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: Zhongyi attended court in the capital, was appointed Right Chancellor of the Ministry of Works, was changed to Duke of Yiguo, and was granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi went to court, became Right Chancellor, was created Duke of Yiguo, and received a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 自海陵遇弑，大軍北還，而窩斡鴟張，命將徂征。

translations.literal: From the time Hailing was assassinated and the great army returned north, while Wowo spread his wings, generals were ordered to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing was assassinated and the main armies marched north, Wowo rose in power and generals were sent against him.

sentences.zh: 及窩斡敗，其黨括裏、紮八奔入于宋，宋人用其謀，侵掠邊鄙，攻取泗、壽、唐、海州。

translations.literal: When Wowo was defeated, his followers Kuoli and Zhaba fled into Song territory; the Song used their plans to raid the frontier and seize Si, Shou, Tang, and Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wowo fell, Kuoli and Zhaba fled to the Song, who used their counsel to raid the frontier and take Si, Shou, Tang, and Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 於是，宋主傳位於宗室子甗，是為宋孝宗，雖嘗遣使來，而欲用敵國禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Song ruler passed the throne to a clansman named Yan; this was Emperor Xiaozong of Song. Though he once sent envoys, he wished to use the protocol of equal states.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor then abdicated to a clansman named Yan—Emperor Xiaozong. Envoys came, but he wanted equal-state protocol.

sentences.zh: 世宗以紇石烈志寧經略宋事，制詔忠義以丞相總戎事，居南京節制諸將，時大定二年也。

translations.literal: Shizong placed Geshilie Zhining in charge of Song affairs and ordered Zhongyi as chancellor to command military affairs, residing at Nanjing to control all generals—this was in the second year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong put Geshilie Zhining in charge of Song affairs and made Zhongyi chancellor-commander at Nanjing to direct all generals, in the second year of Dading.

sentences.zh: 忠義將行，陛辭，上諭之曰：「彼若歸侵疆，貢禮如故，則可罷兵。

translations.literal: As Zhongyi was about to depart he took leave at court; the emperor instructed him, saying, "If they return the invaded territory and tribute gifts remain as before, the army may be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, the emperor told him at court, "If they return invaded lands and tribute resumes as before, you may halt the army."

sentences.zh: 」既至南京，簡閱士卒，分屯要害，戒諸將嚴守備。

translations.literal: Having reached Nanjing, he reviewed the troops, stationed them at key points, and warned the generals to maintain strict defenses.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing he reviewed the troops, posted them at key points, and ordered strict defense.

sentences.zh: 使左副元帥志寧移牒宋樞密使張浚，其略曰：「可還所侵本朝內地，各守自來畫定疆界，凡事一依皇統以來舊約，帥府亦當解嚴。

translations.literal: He had Left Deputy Commander Zhining send a dispatch to Song Privy Council Commissioner Zhang Jun, the gist being, "Return the invaded lands of our dynasty, each side keep the long-established boundaries, all matters follow the old agreements since Huangtong, and the command headquarters will also stand down.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhining write to Song Privy Council Commissioner Zhang Jun: return invaded Jin territory, hold the old boundaries, follow Huangtong agreements, and the command will stand down.

sentences.zh: 如必欲抗衡，請會兵相見。

translations.literal: If you insist on resistance, let us meet in battle.
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on fighting, meet us in the field."

sentences.zh: 」宋宣撫使張浚複書志寧曰：「疆埸之一彼一此，兵家之或勝或負，何常之有，當置勿道。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun replied to Zhining, saying, "That territory shifts back and forth, victory and defeat in war are inconstant—such things should be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun replied that borders shift and victory is inconstant—such matters should be set aside.

sentences.zh: 謹遣官僚，敬造麾下議之。

translations.literal: I respectfully send officials to your command to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He would send officials to Jin headquarters to discuss terms.

sentences.zh: 」是時，已複泗、壽、鄧州，請隳其城，遷其民於宿、亳、蔡州，上曰：「三州本吾土也，得之則已。

translations.literal: At that time Si, Shou, and Deng prefectures had already been recovered; they requested the cities be demolished and the people moved to Su, Bo, and Cai; the emperor said, "The three prefectures were originally our soil; having recovered them is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Si, Shou, and Deng had been recovered; some urged razing the cities and moving the people to Su, Bo, and Cai. The emperor said, "Those lands are ours again; that is enough."

sentences.zh: 」忠義使將士擇善水草休息，且牧馬，俟來歲取淮南。

translations.literal: Zhongyi had the officers and soldiers choose good pasture and water to rest and pasture horses, awaiting next year to take Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi let the troops rest on good pasture and graze horses, planning to take Huainan the next year.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗詔諸將由泗、壽、唐鄧三道進發，宋人聞之，即自方城、葉縣以來田野皆燒夷之，使無所芻牧。

translations.literal: Initially Shizong had ordered the generals to advance by the Si, Shou, Tang, and Deng routes; hearing this, the Song immediately burned the fields from Fangcheng and Ye County onward so there would be no fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong had ordered advances along the Si, Shou, Tang, and Deng routes; the Song burned the countryside from Fangcheng and Ye County so Jin armies would find no fodder.

sentences.zh: 忠義命唐、鄧道軍芻牧許、汝間。

translations.literal: Zhongyi ordered the Tang and Deng route armies to gather fodder between Xu and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi ordered the Tang and Deng columns to forage between Xu and Ru instead.

sentences.zh: 三年，忠義入奏事，遂以丞相兼都元帥。

translations.literal: In the third year Zhongyi entered court to report; he was then made chancellor concurrently Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zhongyi reported at court and was made chancellor and Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 無何，還軍中。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to the army.

sentences.zh: 忠義與宋相持日久，慮夏久雨，弓力易減，宋或乘時見攻，豫選勁弓萬張於別庫。

translations.literal: Zhongyi had long faced the Song and feared that in summer's long rains bow strength would weaken and Song might attack; he therefore selected ten thousand strong bows in a separate storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Facing the Song for so long, he feared summer rains would weaken bows and the Song might attack, so he stored ten thousand strong bows separately.

sentences.zh: 及自汴赴闕議事，次浚州，宋將李世輔果掩取靈璧、虹縣，遂陷宿州。

translations.literal: When he went from Bian to court to discuss affairs and stopped at Junzhou, the Song general Li Shifu indeed raided and took Lingbi and Hong County, and then Suzhou fell.
translations.idiomatic: Going from Bian to court he stopped at Junzhou; Li Shifu then seized Lingbi and Hong County and took Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 忠義使人還汴，發所貯勁弓給志寧軍，與宋人戰，遂大捷，竟複宿州。

translations.literal: Zhongyi sent men back to Bian, issued the stored strong bows to Zhining's army, fought the Song, achieved a great victory, and finally recovered Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi sent men to Bian for the stored bows, armed Zhining's army, won a great victory, and recovered Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 忠義還，以書責宋。

translations.literal: Zhongyi on his return sent a letter reproaching the Song.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Zhongyi sent a letter rebuking the Song.

sentences.zh: 宋同知樞密院事洪遵、計議官盧仲賢，遣使二輩持與志寧書及手狀，歸海、泗、唐、鄧州所侵地，約為叔侄國。

translations.literal: Song Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council Hong Zun and Planning Officer Lu Zhongxian sent two envoys with letters to Zhining and personal notes, returning the invaded lands of Hai, Si, Tang, and Deng and agreeing to a nephew-state relationship.
translations.idiomatic: Song Vice Commissioner Hong Zun and Planning Officer Lu Zhongxian sent envoys with letters to Zhining, offering return of Hai, Si, Tang, and Deng and nephew-state status.

sentences.zh: 報書期十一月使入境，宋又使人來言，禮物未備，請俟十二月行成。

translations.literal: The reply set November for envoys to enter Jin territory; the Song sent word again that gifts were not ready and asked to conclude the treaty in December.
translations.idiomatic: Jin set November for Song envoys to enter; the Song asked to delay until December because gifts were not ready.

sentences.zh: 忠義以其事馳奏，請定書式，且言宋書如式，則許其入界，如其不然，勢須遣還本國，複稟其主，若是往復，動經七八十日，恐誤軍馬進取。

translations.literal: Zhongyi reported urgently, asking to fix the document format, and said if the Song letter matched the format they might enter the border; otherwise they must be sent home to report to their ruler—such back and forth often took seventy or eighty days and might delay the army's advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi reported urgently to fix treaty format, warning that improper Song documents would be sent back and delay campaigns by months.

sentences.zh: 世宗以詔諭之曰：「若宋人歸疆，歲幣如昔，可免奉表稱臣，許世為侄國。

translations.literal: Shizong instructed him by edict, saying, "If the Song return territory and annual tribute remains as before, they may be excused from presenting memorials and calling themselves subjects; they are permitted to be a nephew state for their generation.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong replied that if the Song returned territory and kept tribute, they need not submit memorials as subjects but might remain a nephew state.

sentences.zh: 」忠義乃貽書宋人，前後凡七，宋人他托未從。

translations.literal: Zhongyi then sent letters to the Song, seven in all; the Song made other excuses and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi wrote the Song seven times; they stalled and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 忠義移大軍壓淮境，遣志寧率偏師渡淮，取盱眙、濠、廬、和、滁等州，宋人懼。

translations.literal: Zhongyi moved the main army to press the Huai frontier and sent Zhining with a detached force to cross the Huai and take Xuyi, Hao, Lu, He, Chu, and other prefectures; the Song were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi massed the army on the Huai and sent Zhining across to take Xuyi, Hao, Lu, He, Chu, and other prefectures, alarming the Song.

sentences.zh: 而世宗意天下厭苦兵革，思與百姓休息，詔忠義度宜以行。

translations.literal: But Shizong thought the realm was weary of war and wished rest for the people; he ordered Zhongyi to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, believing the realm was weary of war, ordered Zhongyi to act as circumstances allowed.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，忠義使右監軍宗敘入奏，將近暑月，乞俟秋涼進發。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year Zhongyi sent Right Army Supervisor Zongxu to report at court; as the hot months were near he asked to wait until autumn cool before advancing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Zhongyi sent Right Army Supervisor Zongxu to court, asking to delay advance until autumn cool.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 宋使胡昉敢以右僕射湯思退書來，宋稱侄國，不肯加世字。

translations.literal: The Song envoy Hu Fang dared to come with a letter from Right Vice Director Tang Situ; the Song called themselves a nephew state but refused to add the generational character.
translations.idiomatic: Song envoy Hu Fang brought a letter from Right Vice Director Tang Situ. The Song called themselves a nephew state but refused the generational title.

sentences.zh: 忠義執昉留軍中，答其書，使使以聞。

translations.literal: Zhongyi detained Fang and kept him in the army, replied to his letter, and sent envoys to report.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi detained Fang in camp, answered his letter, and reported to court.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「行人何罪，遣胡昉還國。

translations.literal: An edict said, "What crime has the envoy committed? Send Hu Fang back to his country.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The envoy is not at fault. Send Hu Fang home.

sentences.zh: 邊事從宜措畫。

translations.literal: Border affairs are to be handled as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: Handle border affairs as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 」八月，詔忠義曰：「前請俟秋涼進發，今已八月，複俟何時？

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict to Zhongyi said, "You previously asked to wait for autumn cool before advancing—now it is already the eighth month; how much longer will you wait?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor wrote, "You asked to wait for autumn cool—it is already August. How long will you wait?"

sentences.zh: 」先是，忠義乞增金、銀牌，上曰：「太師梁王兼數職，未嘗增也。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhongyi had requested additional gold and silver tablets; the emperor said, "Grand Preceptor Prince Liang held many offices and never received additions."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhongyi had asked for more command tablets. The emperor said, "Prince Liang held many posts and never asked for more."

sentences.zh: 」至是增都元帥金牌一、銀牌二十，左右副元帥金牌各一、銀牌各十，左右監軍金牌各一、銀牌各六，左右都監金牌各一、銀牌各四，三路都統府銀牌各二。

translations.literal: Now the Commander-in-Chief received one additional gold tablet and twenty silver; each Left and Right Deputy Commander one gold and ten silver; each Left and Right Army Supervisor one gold and six silver; each Left and Right Army Inspector one gold and four silver; each of the three route headquarters two silver tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief received one gold and twenty silver tablets; deputy commanders one gold and ten silver each; army supervisors one gold and six silver; army inspectors one gold and four silver; each route headquarters two silver.

sentences.zh: 乃定南界官員、百姓歸附遷賞格。

translations.literal: Regulations were then set for rewards and promotions when officials and commoners south of the border submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were fixed for officials and people who submitted from the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 元帥府獲宋諜人符忠。

translations.literal: The command headquarters captured the Song spy Fu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters captured the Song spy Fu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠前嘗至中都，大興府官詰問，忠執文據，及與泗州防禦判官張德亨知識，由是獲免，厚謝德亨，德亨受之。

translations.literal: Zhong had once come to the Central Capital; officials of Daxing Prefecture questioned him; Zhong produced documents and knew Suzhou Defense Judge Zhang Deheng, thereby escaping punishment and giving Deheng a rich reward, which Deheng accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong had once reached the Central Capital, produced papers at questioning, and knew Suzhou Judge Zhang Deheng, who helped him escape punishment and accepted a rich bribe.

sentences.zh: 忠具款服，乃奏其事於朝，於是，大興少尹王全解職，德亨除名。

translations.literal: Zhong confessed fully; the matter was reported to court; thereupon Daxing Vice Intendant Wang Quan was removed from office and Deheng was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong confessed; the case went to court; Daxing Vice Intendant Wang Quan was dismissed and Deheng struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 和議始于張浚，中更洪遵、湯思退，及徒單克寧敗宋魏勝於十八裏莊，取楚州，世宗下詔進師，於是宋知樞密院周葵、同知樞密院事王之望書一一如約，和議始定。

translations.literal: Peace talks began with Zhang Jun, passed through Hong Zun and Tang Situ, and when Tudan Kening defeated Song Wei Sheng at Eighteen-li Village and took Chuzhou, Shizong ordered the army forward; then Song Privy Councilor Zhou Kui and Vice Commissioner Wang Zhiwang wrote exactly as agreed, and peace was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Peace began with Zhang Jun, passed through Hong Zun and Tang Situ, and when Tudan Kening defeated Wei Sheng at Eighteen-li Village and took Chuzhou, Shizong advanced the army until Zhou Kui and Wang Zhiwang wrote as agreed and peace was fixed.

sentences.zh: 宋遣試禮部尚書魏杞，崇信軍、承宣使康湑，充通問國信使，取到宋主國書式，並國書副本，宋世為侄國，約歲幣為二十萬兩、匹，國書仍書名再拜，不稱「大」字。

translations.literal: Song sent Acting Minister of Rites Wei Qi and Chongxin Army Commissioner Kang Xu as envoys for communication; they obtained the format of the Song ruler's state letter and a copy; the Song generation was to be a nephew state; annual tribute was set at two hundred thousand taels and bolts; the state letter still bore the name with "respectfully bowing twice" and did not use the character "Great."
translations.idiomatic: Song sent Wei Qi and Kang Xu as envoys with the state-letter format. The Song would be a nephew state, tribute two hundred thousand taels and bolts, letters signed with double obeisance but without the word "Great."

sentences.zh: 大定五年正月，魏杞、康湑入見，其書曰：「侄宋皇帝甗謹再拜致書于叔大金聖明仁孝皇帝闕下。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Dading, Wei Qi and Kang Xu entered audience; the letter read, "Nephew Emperor Yan of Song respectfully bows twice and writes to Uncle Great Jin, the sage, bright, benevolent, and filial Emperor below the steps."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dading year five, Wei Qi and Kang Xu were received. The letter read, "Nephew Emperor Yan of Song respectfully bows twice to Uncle Great Jin, sage, bright, benevolent, and filial Emperor."

sentences.zh: 」魏杞還，複書「叔大金皇帝」不名，不書「謹再拜」，但曰「致書于侄宋皇帝」，不用尊號，不稱闕下。

translations.literal: When Wei Qi returned, the reply read "Uncle Great Jin Emperor" without naming, without "respectfully bowing twice," but only "writes to nephew Emperor of Song," without honorific title or "below the steps."
translations.idiomatic: Jin's reply read "Uncle Great Jin Emperor" without naming or double obeisance, only "writes to nephew Emperor of Song," without honorifics.

sentences.zh: 和好已定，罷兵，詔天下。

translations.literal: Friendly relations were fixed and the armies halted; an edict was issued to all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was fixed, armies stood down, and an edict went to the realm.

sentences.zh: 以左副都點檢完顏仲為報問國信使，太子詹事楊伯雄副之。

translations.literal: Left Deputy Chief Inspector Wanyan Zhong was made returning envoy; Crown Prince Household Minister Yang Boxiong served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Zhong was made returning envoy with Yang Boxiong as deputy.

sentences.zh: 忠義奏官軍一十七萬三千三百餘人，留馬步軍一十一萬六千二百屯戍。

translations.literal: Zhongyi reported government troops at one hundred seventy-three thousand three hundred odd, with one hundred sixteen thousand two hundred horse and foot retained for garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi reported 173,300 government troops with 116,200 horse and foot kept on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「今已許宋講好，而屯戍尚多，可除舊軍外，選馬一萬二千，阿裏喜稱是，步軍虞候司軍共選一萬五千，及簽軍一萬，與舊軍通留六萬。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Now peace with Song is agreed yet garrisons remain numerous; apart from the old army, select twelve thousand horses—Alixi approved—and fifteen thousand from the infantry guard command, plus ten thousand drafted troops, totaling sixty thousand with the old army."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said garrisons were still too large; apart from old troops, keep twelve thousand horses, fifteen thousand infantry guards, ten thousand drafts—sixty thousand in all.
