sentences.zh: 富強丁多者摘留，貧難者阿裏喜官給，富者就用其奴。

translations.literal: Among strong households with many adult males, some were retained; the poor were supplied by Alixi offices; the rich used their own slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Strong households kept more men; the poor were supplied by Alixi offices; the rich used their own retainers.

sentences.zh: 其存留馬步軍于河北東西、大名府、速頻、胡裏改、會甯、咸平府、濟州、東京、曷速館等路軍內，約量揀取。

translations.literal: Retained horse and foot were to be chosen proportionally from armies of Eastern and Western Hebei, Daming, Supin, Huligai, Huining, Xianping, Jizhou, Eastern Capital, and Yisu Hall routes.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons were drawn proportionally from Hebei, Daming, Supin, Huining, Xianping, Jizhou, Eastern Capital, and other routes.

sentences.zh: 其西南、西北招討司，臨潢府、泰州、北京、婆速、曷懶、山東東西路，並行放還。

translations.literal: Southwestern and Northwestern Pacification offices, Linhuang, Taizhou, Beijing, Basu, Yilan, and Eastern and Western Shandong routes were all released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification offices and Linhuang, Taizhou, Beijing, Basu, Yilan, and Shandong forces were all sent home.

sentences.zh: 」詔近侍局使裴滿子寧佩金牌，護衛醜底、符寶祗候駝滿回海佩銀牌，諭諸路將帥，以宋國進到歲幣銀絹二十萬兩、匹，盡數給與見存留及放散軍充賞。

translations.literal: An edict had Palace Attendant Bureau Commissioner Peiman Zining wear a gold tablet and Guard Choudi and Talisman Attendant Tuoman Huihai wear silver tablets, instructing route commanders to distribute the Song tribute of two hundred thousand taels of silver and bolts of silk in full as rewards to retained and discharged troops.
translations.idiomatic: Peiman Zining carried a gold tablet and others silver tablets to distribute Song tribute silver and silk as rewards to retained and discharged troops.

sentences.zh: 曾過界者，人給絹二匹、銀二兩，不曾過界者銀二兩、絹一匹。

translations.literal: Those who had crossed the border received two bolts of silk and two taels of silver per man; those who had not received two taels of silver and one bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had crossed the border received two bolts of silk and two taels of silver; others two taels and one bolt.

sentences.zh: 阿裏喜絹一匹。

translations.literal: Alixi received one bolt of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Alixi officers received one bolt of silk.

sentences.zh: 謀克倍軍人，猛安倍謀克。

translations.literal: Mengke doubled the soldiers; meng'an doubled the mengke.
translations.idiomatic: Mengke units doubled their soldiers; meng'an units doubled their mengke.

sentences.zh: 押軍猛安謀克年老有勞績者，量與除授。

translations.literal: Escort-command meng'an and mengke who were old with merit were given appointments as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Escort meng'an and mengke of age and merit received appointments as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「其令一路全罷者，先發遣之。

translations.literal: Another edict said, "Where an entire route is to be disbanded, send them away first."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said routes to be disbanded entirely should be sent home first.

sentences.zh: 」賜忠義玉束帶。

translations.literal: Zhongyi was granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi received a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔曰：「如大軍已放還，丞相忠義宜先還，左副元帥志寧、右監軍宗敘留駐南京，餘官非急用者並勒還任。」

translations.literal: In the third month an edict said, "If the main army has been released, Chancellor Zhongyi should return first; Left Deputy Commander Zhining and Right Army Supervisor Zongxu remain at Nanjing; other officers not urgently needed are ordered back to their posts."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the edict said if the main army was home, Zhongyi should return first while Zhining and Zongxu stayed at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 忠義朝京師，上勞之曰：「宋國請和，偃兵息民，皆卿力也。

translations.literal: Zhongyi attended court; the emperor comforted him, saying, "The Song sued for peace and arms were laid down for the people—all through your strength.
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor told Zhongyi, "Song peace and rest for the people are your doing alone.

sentences.zh: 」拜左丞相，兼都元帥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor, concurrently Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大定初，事多權制，詔有司刪定，上謂宰臣曰：「凡已奏之事，朕嘗再閱，卿等毋懷懼。

translations.literal: Early in Dading many matters were provisional; an edict ordered offices to revise them; the emperor told the chief ministers, "For every matter already memorialized I read it twice—you need not fear.
translations.idiomatic: Early Dading relied on provisional rules; offices were ordered to revise them. The emperor told ministers, "I read every memorial twice—you need not fear.

sentences.zh: 朕于大臣，豈有不相信者？

translations.literal: How could I not trust my great ministers?
translations.idiomatic: How could I fail to trust my ministers?

sentences.zh: 但軍國事，不敢輕易，恐或有誤也。

translations.literal: But in military and state affairs I dare not be careless, lest there be error."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in military affairs I dare not be careless, lest something go wrong."

sentences.zh: 」忠義對曰：「臣等豈敢竊意陛下，但智力不及耳。

translations.literal: Zhongyi replied, "How would we dare presume upon Your Majesty? Our intelligence simply falls short.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi replied, "We would never presume on Your Majesty—our minds simply fall short.

sentences.zh: 陛下留神萬幾，天下之福也。」

translations.literal: That Your Majesty attends to the myriad affairs is the fortune of all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Your attention to every affair is the realm's fortune."

sentences.zh: 大定六年正月，忠義有疾，上遣太醫診視，賜以御用藥物，中使撫問，相繼於道。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Dading Zhongyi fell ill; the emperor sent imperial physicians, granted imperial medicines, and imperial envoys followed one another on the road with inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhongyi fell ill; imperial physicians and medicines were sent, and envoys followed one another with inquiries.

sentences.zh: 二月，薨。

translations.literal: In the second month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month.

sentences.zh: 上親臨哭之慟，輟朝奠祭，賻銀千五百兩、重彩五十端、絹五百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor came in person to mourn him with deep grief, suspended court for the offering, and granted one thousand five hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of fine silk, and five hundred bolts of plain silk as condolence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him in person, suspended court, and gave 1,500 taels of silver, fifty bolts of fine silk, and five hundred of plain silk.

sentences.zh: 世宗將幸西京，複臨奠焉。

translations.literal: When Shizong was about to visit the Western Capital he again came to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong went to the Western Capital he offered sacrifice again.

sentences.zh: 命參知政事唐括安禮護喪事，凡葬祭從優厚，官為給之。

translations.literal: Participating Administrator Tangguo Anli was ordered to oversee the funeral; all burial and sacrifice rites were generously provided by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Tangguo Anli oversaw the funeral at state expense with full honors.

sentences.zh: 大宗正丞竟充敕祭使，中都轉運副使王震充敕葬使，百官送葬，具一品儀物，建大將旗鼓，送至墳域。

translations.literal: Grand Clan Director Jing Chong served as imperial sacrifice envoy; Central Capital Transport Vice Commissioner Wang Zhen served as imperial burial envoy; all officials escorted the funeral with first-rank rites, great general banners and drums, to the burial ground.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Chong led the sacrifice mission and Wang Zhen the burial mission; officials escorted him with first-rank honors and general's banners to the grave.

sentences.zh: 諡武莊。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Martial and Stately.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Martial and Stately.

sentences.zh: 忠義動由禮義，謙以接下，敬儒士，與人極和易，侃侃如也。

translations.literal: Zhongyi acted from ritual and righteousness, received others with humility, respected scholars, and was extremely easy with people, earnest and open in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi acted from ritual and duty, received men humbly, honored scholars, and was open and easy in manner.

sentences.zh: 善禦將士，能得其死力。

translations.literal: He was skilled in commanding soldiers and could win their utmost loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded soldiers well and won their utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及為宰輔，知無不言。

translations.literal: As chief minister he spoke without reserve on all he knew.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he spoke frankly on everything he knew.

sentences.zh: 自漢、唐以來，外家多緣恩戚以致富貴，又多不克其終，未有兼任將相功名始終如忠義者。

translations.literal: Since Han and Tang, maternal kin often grew rich through favor and kinship yet often could not end well; never had one held both general and minister simultaneously with merit from beginning to end like Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Tang, imperial in-laws often rose by favor and often fell—none had held both command and chancellorship with honor intact like Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔曰：「故左丞相忠義族人，及昭德皇后親族，人材可用者，左副點檢烏古論元忠體察以聞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict said, "Among the clansmen of the late Left Chancellor Zhongyi and the kin of Empress Zhaode, any with usable talent—Left Deputy Inspector Wugulun Yuanzhong is to investigate and report."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the court ordered Yuanzhong to find usable men among Zhongyi's clan and Empress Zhaode's kin.

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，上思忠義功，勒銘墓碑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the emperor, remembering Zhongyi's merit, had an inscription cut on his tombstone.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the emperor had his tomb inscribed in memory of his service.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，圖像衍慶宮，配享世宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe his image was placed in Yansqing Palace and he received posthumous sacrifice in Shizong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year one his portrait entered Yansqing Palace and he was honored in Shizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 子揆，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Huai has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huai has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 徒單合喜

translations.literal: Tudan Hexi
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Hexi

sentences.zh: 徒單合喜，上京速蘇海水人也。

translations.literal: Tudan Hexi was a man of Susuhai River in the Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Hexi came from Susuhai River in the Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 父蒲涅，世襲猛安。

translations.literal: His father Punie held a hereditary meng'an post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Punie held a hereditary meng'an post.

sentences.zh: 合喜魁偉，膂力過人，一經聞見，終身不忘。

translations.literal: Hexi was imposing in stature, with strength surpassing others; what he heard or saw once he never forgot for life.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi was imposing and immensely strong, with a memory that never forgot what he had once seen.

sentences.zh: 天輔間，從金源郡王婁室為紮也，甚愛之。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he followed Prince Jinyuan Loushi as a retainer and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era he followed Prince Jinyuan Loushi as a retainer and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 天會六年，以功為謀克，尋領婁室親管猛安。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhui, for merit he was made mengke and soon led Loushi's personally commanded meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui year six he became mengke for merit and soon led Loushi's personal meng'an.

sentences.zh: 元帥府聞其才，命權左翼軍事。

translations.literal: The command headquarters, hearing of his talent, ordered him to act as left-wing military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters heard of his talent and made him acting left-wing commander.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，為隴州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he was Defense Commissioner of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong year two he was Defense Commissioner of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 以兵十五人敗宋兵二百于高陵，以兵五百人敗宋兵二千于秦州，以兵八百人敗宋兵三千五百於鳳翔。

translations.literal: With fifteen men he defeated two hundred Song troops at Gaoling; with five hundred he defeated two thousand at Qinzhou; with eight hundred he defeated three thousand five hundred at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: With fifteen men he beat two hundred Song troops at Gaoling; with five hundred, two thousand at Qinzhou; with eight hundred, three thousand five hundred at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 以二謀克拒饒風關，宋兵二千來奪其關口，奮擊敗之，諸軍乃得過險。

translations.literal: With two mengke he held Raofeng Pass; two thousand Song troops came to seize the pass; he struck fiercely and defeated them, and the armies were then able to cross the danger.
translations.idiomatic: With two mengke he held Raofeng Pass, beat back two thousand Song troops who tried to take it, and let the army cross.

sentences.zh: 遷平涼尹，再徙臨洮、延安尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Intendant of Pingliang, then again to Intendants of Lintao and Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He became Intendant of Pingliang, then Lintao and Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 是時，關、陝以西，初去兵革，百姓多失業，合喜守之以靜，民多還歸者。

translations.literal: At that time west of Guan and Shaanxi had just left warfare behind; many common people had lost their livelihoods; Hexi kept them through quiet rule and many people returned.
translations.idiomatic: West of the passes had just seen war end; Hexi ruled quietly and people returned.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，為元帥左都監，陝西統軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was Left Army Inspector of the Commander-in-Chief and Shaanxi Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande year two he was Left Army Inspector and Shaanxi commander.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，以本官兼河中尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan he held the same office concurrently as Intendant of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan year two he was also Intendant of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 正隆六年，為西蜀道兵馬都統。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenglong he was Commander-in-Chief of Western Shu Route forces.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong year six he commanded Western Shu forces.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以手詔賜合喜曰：「岐國失道，殺其母后，橫虐兄弟，流毒兆庶。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne he sent a personal edict to Hexi, saying, "The Qi state lost the Way, killed its empress dowager, abused his brothers, and spread poison among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded he wrote Hexi, "The Qi ruler lost the Way, killed his empress dowager, abused his brothers, and poisoned the people.

sentences.zh: 朕惟太祖創業之艱難，勉膺大位。

translations.literal: I alone recall the hardship of Taizu's founding and have reluctantly accepted the great throne.
translations.idiomatic: I recall Taizu's founding hardships and have taken the throne.

sentences.zh: 卿之子弟皆自軍中來歸，卿國家舊臣，豈不知天道人事？

translations.literal: Your sons and younger brothers have all returned from the army; you are an old servant of the state—do you not know Heaven's will and human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Your kin have returned from the armies. As an old servant of the state, do you not know Heaven's will?

sentences.zh: 卿軍不多，未宜深入，當領軍屯境上。

translations.literal: Your army is not large and should not penetrate deeply; you should lead the army to encamp on the border.
translations.idiomatic: Your force is small—do not advance deep, but hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 陝右重地，非卿無能措畫者。

translations.literal: The land west of Shaanxi is vital; without you no one can plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi is vital; none but you can manage it.

sentences.zh: 俟兵革既定，即當召卿，宜自勉之。

translations.literal: When arms are settled I shall summon you—strive on your own behalf."
translations.idiomatic: When war ends I shall recall you—do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 」大定二年，複為陝西路統軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he again became Shaanxi Route Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading year two he again commanded Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改元帥右都監。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Right Army Inspector of the Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Right Army Inspector.

sentences.zh: 表陳伐宋方略，詔許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: He memorialized a plan to attack Song; an edict permitted him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a Song campaign plan and was allowed discretion.

sentences.zh: 轉左都監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Army Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Army Inspector.

sentences.zh: 破宋兵于華州。

translations.literal: He defeated Song troops at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Song troops at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 是時宋吳璘侵古鎮，分據散關、和尚原、神叉口、玉女潭、大蟲嶺、石壁寨、寶雞縣，兵十余萬，陷河州、鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: At that time Song Wu Lin raided Guzhen, held San Pass, Heshang Plain, Shencha Pass, Jade Maiden Pool, Great Worm Ridge, Stone Wall Fort, and Baoji County with more than a hundred thousand men, and captured Hezhou and Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin held passes from San Pass to Baoji with over 100,000 men and took Hezhou and Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 合喜乞濟師，詔以河南兵萬人益之。

translations.literal: Hexi requested reinforcements; an edict added ten thousand Henan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi asked for help and received ten thousand Henan troops.

sentences.zh: 合喜遣丹州刺史赤盞胡速魯改以兵四千守德順，吳璘以二十萬人圍之。

translations.literal: Hexi sent Danzhou Prefect Chizan Husulugai with four thousand men to hold De Shun; Wu Lin surrounded it with two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi sent Husulugai with four thousand to hold De Shun; Wu Lin besieged it with 200,000.

sentences.zh: 統軍都監石抹迭勒將兵萬人，破宋兵於河州，還過德順，駐兵平涼，求益兵於合喜，以解德順之圍。

translations.literal: Army Inspector Shimodie led ten thousand men, defeated Song troops at Hezhou, passed De Shun, encamped at Pingliang, and asked Hexi for more troops to relieve De Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Shimodie beat Song forces at Hezhou, camped at Pingliang, and asked Hexi for more men to relieve De Shun.

sentences.zh: 合喜遣萬戶完顏習尼列、大良順，甯州刺史顏盞門都各將本部兵，合二萬人，以順義軍節度使烏延蒲離黑統押之，與迭勒會。

translations.literal: Hexi sent Commanders Wanyan Xini Lie and Daliang Shun and Ningzhou Prefect Yanzhan Mendu, each with his own troops totaling twenty thousand, under Shunyi Military Commissioner Wuyan Pulihai as overall commander, to join Shimodie.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi sent Xini Lie, Daliang Shun, and Mendu with twenty thousand under Pulihai to join Shimodie.

sentences.zh: 吳璘聞之，使偏將將兵五千人來迎，前鋒特裏失烏也、奚王和尚擊敗之，追至德順城南小溪邊，璘自將大軍蔽岡阜而出，烏也等馳擊之，迭勒、蒲離黑繼至，並力戰，日已暮，兩軍不相辨，乃解。

translations.literal: Wu Lin heard and sent a subordinate with five thousand to meet them; vanguard Telisi Wuye and Xi Prince Heshang defeated them and pursued to the brook south of De Shun; Lin himself led the main army out from behind the hill; Wuye and others charged; Shimodie and Pulihai arrived and all fought together; by evening the two armies could not distinguish one another and disengaged.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin sent five thousand to meet them; Wuye and Heshang routed them; at dusk Lin led the main force out and battle blurred until nightfall.

sentences.zh: 已而璘報雲：「宋主遣使至，兩國講和，請各罷兵。

translations.literal: Before long Lin reported, "The Song ruler has sent envoys; the two states are making peace—let each side withdraw its army."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin then reported that Song envoys had come and both sides should withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」璘遂遁去。

translations.literal: Lin thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Lin fled.

sentences.zh: 蒲離黑亦引軍還。

translations.literal: Pulihai also withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Pulihai withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 自宋兵圍城，至是凡四十余日乃解。

translations.literal: From the time the Song besieged the city until then more than forty days had passed before the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege had lasted more than forty days before it was lifted.

sentences.zh: 初，德順在圍中，押軍猛安溫敦蒲里海身先士卒，力戰未嘗少挫，及救兵至，圍解，蒲里海之功為多。

translations.literal: Initially, while De Shun was besieged, escort meng'an Wendun Pulihai led from the front, fought fiercely without slackening, and when relief arrived and the siege was lifted Pulihai's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege Wendun Pulihai fought at the front without slackening and earned the greatest credit when relief came.

sentences.zh: 頃之，吳璘複來犯陝西州郡，兵十余萬。

translations.literal: Before long Wu Lin again came to attack Shaanxi prefectures and counties with more than a hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wu Lin attacked Shaanxi again with over 100,000 men.

sentences.zh: 詔以兵七千益合喜兵，號二萬人，慶陽尹烏延蒲轄奴、延安尹高景山分領之。

translations.literal: An edict added seven thousand troops to Hexi's army, making twenty thousand in name; Qingyang Intendant Wuyan Puxianu and Yan'an Intendant Gao Jingshan each commanded a division.
translations.idiomatic: Seven thousand more men were added, bringing Hexi's force to twenty thousand under Puxianu and Gao Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 彰化軍節度使璋、通遠軍節度使烏延吾裏補、甯州刺史移剌高山奴、京兆少尹宗室泥河、恩州刺史完顏謀良虎，皆備軍前任使。

translations.literal: Zhanghua Military Commissioner Zhang, Tongyuan Military Commissioner Wuyan Wulibu, Ningzhou Prefect Yila Gaoshannu, Jingzhao Vice Intendant clansman Nihe, and Enzhou Prefect Wanyan Moulianghu all prepared their armies and took up prior assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Wulibu, Gaoshannu, Nihe, and Moulianghu took their commands.

sentences.zh: 宋人驅率商、虢及華山、南山之民五萬人，來圍華州。

translations.literal: The Song drove fifty thousand people of Shang, Guo, and the Huashan and southern mountains to surround Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Song drove fifty thousand civilians from Shang, Guo, and the southern mountains to besiege Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 押軍萬戶裴滿挼剌欲堅壁守之，猛安移剌沙裏剌曰：「宋兵雖多，半是居民，不習戰，不如擊之。

translations.literal: Escort Commander Peiman Aola wished to hold the walls; meng'an Yila Shalila said, "Though the Song are many, half are civilians who do not know war—it is better to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Peiman Aola wanted to hold the walls; Yila Shalila said half the Song host were untrained civilians and they should attack.

sentences.zh: 」於是挼剌以騎兵千人敗宋前鋒，追至其大軍，亦敗之，斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: Thereupon Aola with one thousand cavalry defeated the Song vanguard, pursued to the main army, defeated that as well, and beheaded more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Aola with a thousand horsemen routed the vanguard and main Song force, taking more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 已而，璋敗宋姚良輔軍于原州，宋戍軍自寶雞以西，至於大蟲嶺，皆自散關遁去。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang defeated Song Yao Liangfu's army at Yuanzhou; Song garrisons from west of Baoji to Great Worm Ridge all fled through San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang beat Yao Liangfu at Yuanzhou, and Song garrisons west of Baoji fled through San Pass.

sentences.zh: 頃之，吳璘聞赤盞胡速魯改、烏延蒲裏黑軍已去德順，率兵號二十萬，複據德順，陷鞏州、臨洮府。

translations.literal: Before long Wu Lin, hearing that Chizan Husulugai and Wuyan Pulihai's armies had left De Shun, led a force claiming two hundred thousand, again held De Shun, and captured Gongzhou and Lintao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Jin forces had left De Shun, Wu Lin returned with 200,000 men, retook De Shun, and took Gongzhou and Lintao.

sentences.zh: 臨洮少尹紇石烈騷洽死之，詔贈官一階，賜錢五百貫。

translations.literal: Lintao Vice Intendant Geshilie Saoqia died in the defense; an edict promoted his rank one step and granted five hundred strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Saoqia died defending Lintao and was posthumously promoted with five hundred strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 合喜以璋權都統，習尼列權副統，將兵二萬攻之。

translations.literal: Hexi made Zhang acting commander-in-chief and Xini Lie acting deputy, and attacked with twenty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi made Zhang acting commander and Xini Lie deputy and attacked with twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 連戰，宋兵雖敗，璘恃其眾，不肯去，分其兵之半，守秦州。

translations.literal: After repeated battles the Song army was defeated, yet Lin relied on his numbers and would not leave, dividing half his force to hold Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Battle followed battle and the Song were beaten, but Wu Lin trusted his numbers, refused to withdraw, and left half his army to hold Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 合喜乃自行，駐水洛城，東自六盤山，西抵石山頭，分兵守之，當德順、秦州之兩間，斷其餉道，璘乃引去。

translations.literal: Hexi then went in person, encamped at Shuiluo City, posted troops from Liupan Mountain in the east to Stone Mountain Head in the west, divided forces to hold them, stood between De Shun and Qinzhou, cut off their supply route, and Lin thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hexi took the field himself, encamped at Shuiluo, and posted troops from Liupan Mountain east to Stone Mountain Head west, cutting Wu Lin's supply line between De Shun and Qinzhou until Lin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 都統璋、副統習尼列邀擊宋經略使荊皋，自上八節至甘穀城，殺數千人。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Zhang and Deputy Commander Xini Lie intercepted Song Pacification Commissioner Jing Gao from Upper Eight Sections to Gangu City and killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Xini Lie intercepted Song Commissioner Jing Gao from Upper Eight Sections to Gangu City and killed several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 習尼列擒宋將硃永以下將校十二人。

translations.literal: Xini Lie captured the Song general Zhu Yong and eleven other officers below him.
translations.idiomatic: Xini Lie captured Song general Zhu Yong and eleven other officers.

sentences.zh: 宋張安撫守德順，亦棄城遁，胡速魯改邀擊之，所殺過半，擒將校十餘人，遂複德順州。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang, holding De Shun, also abandoned the city and fled; Husulugai intercepted them, killed more than half, captured more than ten officers, and thereby recovered De Shun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang also fled De Shun; Husulugai intercepted the fugitives, killed more than half, took a dozen officers, and recovered De Shun.

sentences.zh: 宋之守秦州者，亦自退。

translations.literal: The Song garrison at Qinzhou also withdrew on its own.
translations.idiomatic: The Song garrison at Qinzhou withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 高景山定商、虢，宗室泥河取環州。

translations.literal: Gao Jingshan pacified Shang and Guo; clansman Nihe took Huanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jingshan secured Shang and Guo; clansman Nihe took Huanzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是，臨洮、鞏、秦、河、隴、蘭、會、原、洮、積石、鎮戎、德順、商、虢、環、華等州府一十六盡複之，陝西平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the sixteen prefectures and districts of Lintao, Gong, Qin, He, Long, Lan, Hui, Yuan, Tao, Jishi, Zhenrong, De Shun, Shang, Guo, Huan, and Hua were all recovered and Shaanxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All sixteen prefectures from Lintao to Hua were recovered and Shaanxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔書獎諭，賜以玉帶。

translations.literal: An edict commended him and granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised his service and gave him a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 詔陝西將士，猛安，階昭毅以下遷兩資，昭武以上遷一資。

translations.literal: An edict to Shaanxi officers and soldiers: meng'an of rank Zhao Yi and below were promoted two steps; Zhao Wu and above one step.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi meng'an of Zhao Yi rank and below were promoted two steps; Zhao Wu and above one step.

sentences.zh: 謀克，階六品以下遷兩資，五品以上遷一資。

translations.literal: Mengke of sixth rank and below were promoted two steps; fifth rank and above one step.
translations.idiomatic: Mengke of sixth rank and below gained two steps; fifth rank and above one step.

sentences.zh: 押軍猛安，階昭武以上者遷一資，昭毅以下、武義以上遷兩資，昭信以下，女直人遷宣武，餘人遷奉信，無官者，女直人授敦信，餘人授忠武。

translations.literal: Escort meng'an of Zhao Wu and above were promoted one step; Zhao Yi and below but Wu Yi and above two steps; Zhao Xin and below—Jurchen were promoted to Xuanwu, others to Fengxin; those without office—Jurchen received Dunxin, others Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Escort meng'an were promoted by rank; Jurchen without office received Dunxin, others Zhongwu, according to detailed regulations.

sentences.zh: 押軍謀克，武功以下、忠顯以上遷兩資，忠勇以下，女直人遷昭信，餘人遷忠顯，無官者，女直人授忠顯，餘人授忠翊。

translations.literal: Escort mengke of Wu Gong and below but Zhong Xian and above were promoted two steps; Zhong Yong and below—Jurchen to Zhao Xin, others to Zhong Xian; without office—Jurchen received Zhong Xian, others Zhong Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Escort mengke received similar promotions by rank, with separate provisions for Jurchen and others without prior office.

sentences.zh: 正軍，有官者遷一資，無官者授兩資。

translations.literal: Regular soldiers: those with office were promoted one step; those without received two steps.
translations.idiomatic: Regular soldiers with rank gained one step; those without rank received two.

sentences.zh: 猛安賞銀五十兩、重彩五端、絹十匹，權、正同之。

translations.literal: Meng'an were rewarded fifty taels of silver, five bolts of fine silk, and ten bolts of plain silk; acting and regular posts alike.
translations.idiomatic: Each meng'an received fifty taels of silver, five bolts of fine silk, and ten of plain silk, whether acting or regular.

sentences.zh: 正軍人給錢三十貫，阿裏喜十貫。

translations.literal: Regular soldiers were given thirty strings of cash; Alixi ten strings.
translations.idiomatic: Regular soldiers received thirty strings of cash; Alixi officers ten.

sentences.zh: 戰沒軍官、軍士、長行，贈官賜錢有差。

translations.literal: Officers, soldiers, and camp followers who died in battle received posthumous ranks and cash gifts in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men killed in battle received posthumous honors and cash in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 五年，置陝西路統軍使，兼京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Shaanxi Route Commander-in-Chief was established, concurrently Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Shaanxi Route commander, concurrently Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 元帥府移治河中府。

translations.literal: The command headquarters was moved to Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters moved to Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 統軍使璋朝辭，上曰：「合喜年老，以陝西軍事委卿，凡鎮防利害，可訪問合喜也。

translations.literal: Commander Zhang took leave at court; the emperor said, "Hexi is old; I entrust Shaanxi military affairs to you—for all garrison advantages and dangers you may consult Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang took leave at court the emperor said, "Hexi is old; I leave Shaanxi to you. On every point of frontier defense, consult him."

sentences.zh: 」七年，入為樞密副使，改東京留守，賜以衣帶、佩刀，詔曰：「卿年老，以此職優佚，宜勉之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered court as Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, was changed to Regent of the Eastern Capital, and granted robes, belt, and belt knife; an edict said, "You are old; with this post as a comfortable ease you should strive on.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he became Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council and Regent of the Eastern Capital, with robes, belt, and knife. The edict said, "You are old; this post is meant as ease—do your best nonetheless."

sentences.zh: 」九年，入為平章政事，奏睿宗收復陝西功數事，上嘉納之，藏之秘府。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered as Grand Councilor, memorialized several matters concerning Prince Ruizong's recovery of Shaanxi merit; the emperor praised and accepted them and stored them in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Grand Councilor and memorialized Ruizong's Shaanxi campaigns; the emperor approved and filed the memorials in the secret archive.

sentences.zh: 封定國公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was created Duke of Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 十一年，薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 上方擊球，聞訃遂罷。

translations.literal: The emperor was playing ball; hearing the news of his death he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at ball when he heard the news and stopped the game.

sentences.zh: 有司致祭，備禮以葬。

translations.literal: The relevant offices performed sacrifices and buried him with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: The court performed the rites and buried him with full honors.

sentences.zh: 賻銀一千二百五十兩及重彩幣帛。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts of one thousand two hundred fifty taels of silver and fine silk goods.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence gifts of 1,250 taels of silver and fine silks were granted.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，上念其功，遷其孫三合武功將軍，授世襲本猛安曷懶若窟申謀克。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the emperor, remembering his merit, promoted his grandson Sanhe to Military Merit General and granted the hereditary meng'an Yilan Ruokushen mengke of his original post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the emperor promoted his grandson Sanhe to Military Merit General and granted him the hereditary meng'an post.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，配享世宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taihe he received posthumous sacrifice in Shizong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year one he was honored in Shizong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：大定之初，兵連于江、淮，難作於契丹，謀衍挾功，窩斡橫噬，有弗戢之畏焉。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Early in Dading, arms were joined on the Yangtze and Huai; trouble arose among the Khitan; Moyan relied on his merit; Wowo ravaged unchecked—there was fear that they could not be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Early in Dading war ran along the Yangtze and Huai, Khitan rebellion flared, Moyan clung to his victories, and Wowo ravaged unchecked—fear that none could be stopped.

sentences.zh: 世宗獨斷，召還謀衍，僕散忠義受任責成矣。

translations.literal: Shizong decided alone, recalled Moyan, and Pusan Zhongyi received the commission and fulfilled the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong acted decisively, recalled Moyan, and entrusted the task to Pusan Zhongyi, who carried it through.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「兵主於將，將賢則士勇。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, "Armies depend on their generals; when the general is worthy the soldiers are brave.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying, "Armies depend on their generals; worthy generals make brave soldiers."

sentences.zh: 」其此之謂邪！

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant!"
translations.idiomatic: Is this not exactly the case?

sentences.zh: 紇石烈志寧有言：「受詔征伐，則不敢辭，為宰相則誠不能。

translations.literal: Geshilie Zhining once said, "When I receive an edict to campaign I dare not refuse; as chancellor I truly cannot manage it.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Zhining once said, "Ordered to war, I do not refuse; asked to be chancellor, I truly cannot."

sentences.zh: 」如知為相之難，固所謂賢也。

translations.literal: To know the difficulty of being chancellor—this is indeed what is called worthiness.
translations.idiomatic: To know the difficulty of high office is itself a kind of wisdom.

sentences.zh: 秦、隴之兵，殆哉岌岌乎，徒單合喜料敵應變若此之審，亦難矣哉。

translations.literal: The armies of Qin and Long were perilous, teetering on the edge; that Tudan Hexi could gauge the enemy and respond to change with such precision was also a rare achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Qin and Long stood in peril; that Tudan Hexi could read the enemy and adapt with such precision was no small feat.
